creator: Bidwan Chakraborty † and Mousumi Mandal ∗
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bidwan Chakraborty † and Mousumi Mandal ∗. Let G n , r G_{n,r} denote the graph with n n vertices { x 1 , … , x n } \{x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\} in cyclic order and for each vertex x i x_{i} consider the set A i = { x i − r , … , x i − 1 , x i + 1 , x i + 2 , … , x i + r } , A_{i}=\{x_{i-r},\ldots,x_{i-1},x_{i+1},x_{i+2},\ldots,x_{i+r}\}, where x i − j x_{i-j}

title: Broadband Emission from a Kilonova Ejecta-Pulsar Wind Nebula System: Late-Time X-ray Afterglow Rebrightening of GRB 170817A 2021 Broadband Emission from a Kilonova Ejecta-Pulsar Wind Nebula System: Late-Time X-ray Afterglow Rebrightening of GRB 170817A – 4
creator: J. Ren, Z. G. Dai
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by J. Ren, Z. G. Dai. We study the broadband radiation behavior of a kilonova ejecta-pulsar wind nebula (PWN) system. In this model, we jointly fit the observations of AT 2017gfo in UV-optical-IR bands and the late-time X-ray afterglow of GRB 170817A. Our work shows that a PWN powered by the remnant neutron star (NS) post GW170817 event could affect the optical transient AT 2017gfo and re-brighten the late-time X-ray afterglow of GRB 170817A.

title: Conservativity spectra and generalized Ignatiev model Thanks: This work was performed at the Steklov International Mathematical Center and supported by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation (agreement no. 075-15-2019-1614).
creator: Lev D. Beklemishev
description: Abstract We study a generalization of the notion of conservativity spectrum of an arithmetical theory to a language with transfinitely many truth definitions introduced in [ 1 ] . We establish a correspondence of conservativity spectra and points of a generalized Ignatied model introduced and studied by D. Fernández-Duque and J. Joosten.

title: On some properties of ω \omega -uniqueness in tensor complementarity problem
creator: A. Dutta, R. Deb, A. K. Das
description: Abstract In this article we introduce column adequate tensor in the context of tensor complementarity problem and consider some important properties. The tensor complementarity problem is a class of nonlinear complematarity problems with the involved function being defined by a tensor. We establish the inheritance property and invariant property of column adequate tensors.

title: Theory of scanning gate microscopy imaging of the supercurrent distribution in a planar Josephson junction
creator: K. Kaperek, S. Heun, M. Carrega, P. Wójcik, M. P. Nowak
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by K. Kaperek, S. Heun, M. Carrega, P. Wójcik, M. P. Nowak. We theoretically investigate the mapping of the supercurrent distribution in a planar superconductor-normal-superconductor junction in the presence of a perpendicular magnetic field via the scanning gate microscopy technique. We find that the distribution of counter-propagating supercurrents aligned in Josephson vortices can be mapped by the change of the critical current induced by the tip of the scanning probe, if the flux in the junction is set close to maxima of the Fraunhofer pattern.

title: On the complexity of the word problem of the R.​ Thompson group V V
creator: J.C. Birget
description: Abstract We analyze the proof by Lehnert and Schweitzer that the word problem of the Thompson group V V is co-context-free, and we show that this word problem is the complement of the cyclic closure of a union of reverse deterministic context-free languages.

title: Kepler Pixel Project – background RR Lyrae stars in the primary Kepler mission field of view Journal: ApJS Facilities: Kepler, Gaia Python ( Van Rossum & Drake 2009 ) , AstroPy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , astroML ( Vanderplas et al. 2012 ) , LightKurve ( Lightkurve Collaboration et al. 2
creator: Adrienn Forró, Róbert Szabó, Attila Bódi, Kornél Császár
description: Abstract In this paper we describe a project we initiated to investigate individual pixels in the downloaded K ​ e ​ p ​ l ​ e ​ r Kepler apertures in order to find objects in the background of the main targets with variable brightness.

title: Laplacian Filters for Integral Equations: Further Developments and Fast Algorithms
creator: Francesco P. Andriulli
description: Abstract This paper extends the concept of Laplacian filtered quasi-Helmholtz decompositions we have recently introduced, to the basis-free projector-based setting. This extension allows the discrete analyses of electromagnetic integral operators spectra without passing via an explicit Loop-Star decomposition as previously done.

title: Triangular modular curves of small genus
creator: Juanita Duque-Rosero, John Voight
description: Abstract . Triangular modular curves are a generalization of modular curves that arise from quotients of the upper half-plane by congruence subgroups of hyperbolic triangle groups. These curves also arise naturally as a source of Belyi maps with monodromy PGL 2 ​ ( 𝔽 q ) \text{PGL}_{2}(\mathbb{F}_{q}) or PSL 2 ​ ( 𝔽 q ) \text{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{F}_{q}) .

title: Cloud-convection feedback in brown dwarfs atmosphere
creator: Maxence Lefèvre, Xianyu Tan, Elspeth K. H. Lee, R. T. Pierrehumbert
description: Abstract Abstract Numerous observational evidence has suggested the presence of active meteorology in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs. A near-infrared brightness variability has been observed. Clouds have a major role in shaping the thermal structure and spectral properties of these atmospheres.

title: Linear and nonlinear waves in quantum plasmas with arbitrary degeneracy of electrons
creator: Fernando Haas, Shahzad Mahmood
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fernando Haas, Shahzad Mahmood. The purpose of this review is to revisit recent results in the literature where quantum plasmas with arbitrary degeneracy degree are considered. This is different from a frequent approach, where completely degeneracy is assumed in dense plasmas. The general reasoning in the reviewed works is to take a numerical coefficient in from of the Bohm potential term in quantum fluids, in order to fit the linear waves from quantum kinetic theory in the long wavelength limit.

title: A spectroscopic survey of infrared 1-4 µ \boldsymbol{\micro} m spectra in regions of prominent solar coronal emission lines of Fe XIII, Si X, and Si IX Journal: ApJ
creator: Aatiya Ali, Alin Razvan Paraschiv, Kevin Reardon, Philip Judge
description: Abstract The infrared solar spectrum contains a wealth of physical data about the Sun and is being explored using modern detectors and technology with new ground-based solar telescopes. One such instrument will be the ground-based Cryogenic Near-IR Spectro-Polarimeter of the Daniel K.

title: Adversarial Learned Fair Representations using Dampening and Stacking
creator: Max Knobbout
description: Abstract As more decisions in our daily life become automated, the need to have machine learning algorithms that make fair decisions increases. In fair representation learning we are tasked with finding a suitable representation of the data in which a sensitive variable is censored. Recent work aims to learn fair representations through adversarial learning.

title: Measurability of functionals and of ideal point forecasts
creator: Tobias Fissler, Hajo Holzmann
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tobias Fissler, Hajo Holzmann. The ideal probabilistic forecast for a random variable Y Y based on an information set ℱ \mathcal{F} is the conditional distribution of Y Y given ℱ \mathcal{F} . In the context of point forecasts aiming to specify a functional T T such as the mean, a quantile or a risk measure, the ideal point forecast is the respective functional applied to the conditional distribution.

title: Intrinsic randomness under general quantum measurements
creator: Hao Dai, Boyang Chen, Xingjian Zhang, Xiongfeng Ma
description: Abstract Quantum measurements can produce randomness arising from the uncertainty principle. When measuring a state with von Neumann measurements, the intrinsic randomness can be quantified by the quantum coherence of the state on the measurement basis. Unlike projection measurements, there are additional and possibly hidden degrees of freedom in apparatus for generic measurements.

title: The Structured Abstain Problem and the Lovász Hinge
description: Abstract The Lovász hinge is a convex surrogate recently proposed for structured binary classification, in which k k binary predictions are made simultaneously and the error is judged by a submodular set function. Despite its wide usage in image segmentation and related problems, its consistency has remained open.

title: Long-time existence for systems of quasilinear wave equations Thanks: The first author was supported in part by Simons Foundation Collaboration Grant 711724 and NSF grant DMS-2054910.
creator: Jason Metcalfe, Taylor Rhoads
description: Abstract . We consider quasilinear wave equations in ( 1 + 3 ) (1+3) -dimensions where the nonlinearity F ⁡ ( u , u ′ , u ′′ ) F(u,u^{\prime},u^{\prime\prime}) is permitted to depend on the solution rather than just its derivatives.

title: Context-Aware Drift Detection
creator: Oliver Cobb, Arnaud Van Looveren
description: Abstract When monitoring machine learning systems, two-sample tests of homogeneity form the foundation upon which existing approaches to drift detection build. They are used to test for evidence that the distribution underlying recent deployment data differs from that underlying the historical reference data.

title: Counterfactual Inference of Second Opinions
creator: Nina L. Corvelo Benz, Manuel Gomez Rodriguez
description: Abstract Automated decision support systems that are able to infer second opinions from experts can potentially facilitate a more efficient allocation of resources—they can help decide when and from whom to seek a second opinion. In this paper, we look at the design of this type of support systems from the perspective of counterfactual inference.

title: Diagnosing Circumburst Environment with Multiband Gamma-Ray Burst Radio Afterglows Journal: ApJ
creator: Bo Zhang, Liang-Duan Liu, Tian-Rui Sun, Fen Lyu, Xue-Feng Wu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bo Zhang, Liang-Duan Liu, Tian-Rui Sun, Fen Lyu, Xue-Feng Wu. It has been widely recognized that gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows arise from interactions between the GRB outflow and circumburst medium, while their evolution follows the behaviors of relativistic shock waves.

title: Cutoff in the Bernoulli-Laplace model with O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) swaps
creator: Joseph S. Alameda, Caroline Bang, Zachary Brennan, David P. Herzog, Jürgen Kritschgau, Elizabeth Sprangel
description: Abstract This paper considers the ( n , k ) (n,k) -Bernoulli–Laplace model in the case when there are two urns, the total number of red and white balls is the same, and the number of selections k k at each step is on the same asymptotic order as the number of balls n n in each urn.

title: Bias in multivariable Mendelian randomization studies due to measurement error on exposures
creator: Jiazheng Zhu, Stephen Burgess, Andrew J. Grant
description: Abstract Multivariable Mendelian randomization estimates the causal effect of multiple exposures on an outcome, typically using summary statistics of genetic variant associations. However, exposures of interest in Mendelian randomization applications will often be measured with error. The summary statistics will therefore not be of the genetic associations with the exposure, but with the exposure measured with error.

title: A Liouville type result and quantization effects on the system − Δ ​ u = u ​ J ′ ​ ( 1 − | u | 2 ) -\Delta u=uJ^{\prime}(1-|u|^{2}) for a potential convex near zero
creator: U. De Maio, R. Hadiji, and C. Lefter, C. Perugia
description: Abstract We consider a Ginzburg-Landau type equation in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} of the form − Δ ​ u = u ​ J ′ ​ ( 1 − | u | 2 ) -\Delta u=uJ^{\prime}(1-|u|^{2}) with a potential function J J satisfying weak conditions allowing for example a zero of infinite order in the origin.

title: Neutron stars as photon double-lenses: constraining resonant conversion into ALPs Journal: Physics Letters B
creator: Kyrylo Bondarenko, Alexey Boyarsky, Josef Pradler, Anastasia Sokolenko
description: Abstract Axion-photon conversion is a prime mechanism to detect axion-like particles that share a coupling to the photon. We point out that in the vicinity of neutron stars with strong magnetic fields, magnetars, the effective photon mass receives comparable but opposite contributions from free electrons and the radiation field.

title: Measuring Fairness of Text Classifiers via Prediction Sensitivity
creator: Satyapriya Krishna, Rahul Gupta, Apurv Verma
description: Abstract With the rapid growth in language processing applications, fairness has emerged as an important consideration in data-driven solutions. Although various fairness definitions have been explored in the recent literature, there is lack of consensus on which metrics most accurately reflect the fairness of a system.

title: Decoupled Knowledge Distillation
creator: Borui Zhao, Quan Cui, Renjie Song, Yiyu Qiu, Jiajun Liang
description: Abstract State-of-the-art distillation methods are mainly based on distilling deep features from intermediate layers, while the significance of logit distillation is greatly overlooked. To provide a novel viewpoint to study logit distillation, we reformulate the classical KD loss into two parts, i.e . , target class knowledge distillation (TCKD) and non-target class knowledge distillation (NCKD).

title: How to construct Gorenstein projective modules relative to complete duality pairs over Morita rings
creator: Yajun Ma, Jiafeng L
description: Abstract \bf Abstract Let \Delta=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&{{}_{A}N_{B}}\\ {{}_{B}M_{A}}&B\\ \end{smallmatrix}\right) be a Morita ring with M\otimes_{A}N=0=N\otimes_{B}M . We first study how to construct (complete) duality pairs of \Delta -modules using (complete) duality pairs of A -modules and B -modules, generalizing the result of Mao (Comm. Algebra, 2020, 12: 5296–5310) about the duality pairs over a triangular matrix ring.

title: Fast and efficient demultiplexing of single photons from a quantum dot with resonantly enhanced electro-optic modulators
creator: Julian Münzberg, Franz Draxl, Saimon Filipe Covre da Silva, Yusuf Karli, Santanu Manna, Armando Rastelli, Gregor Weihs, Robert Keil
description: Abstract We report on a multi-photon source based on active demultiplexing of single photons emitted from a resonantly excited GaAs quantum dot. Active temporal-to-spatial mode demultipexing is implemented via resonantly enhanced free-space electro-optic modulators, making it possible to route individual photons at high switching rates of 38 MHz 38\text{\,}\mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z} .

title: A Feasibility Study of Answer-Agnostic Question Generation for Education
creator: Liam Dugan, Eleni Miltsakaki, Shriyash Upadhyay, Etan Ginsberg
description: Abstract We conduct a feasibility study into the applicability of answer-agnostic question generation models to textbook passages. We show that a significant portion of errors in such systems arise from asking irrelevant or uninterpretable questions and that such errors can be ameliorated by providing summarized input.

title: Sniper Backdoor: Single Client Targeted Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning Thanks: The Horizon Europe, Spanish CDTI, and ELKARTEK programs partially fund this research. Grant agreements 101021911 (IDUNN), CER-20191012 (EGIDA), and KK-2021/00091 (REMEDY), respectively.
creator: Gorka Abad 2 3 , Servio Paguada 2 3 , Oğuzhan Ersoy 2 , Stjepan Picek 2 , Víctor Julio Ramírez-Durán 3 and Aitor Urbieta 3
description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of Deep Learning (DL) models where the data is retained locally. Like DL, FL has severe security weaknesses that the attackers can exploit, e.g., model inversion and backdoor attacks. Model inversion attacks reconstruct the data from the training datasets, whereas backdoors misclassify only classes containing specific properties, e.g., a pixel pattern.

title: Core overshoot constrained by the absence of a solar convective core and some solar-like stars 2020 Core overshoot constrained by the absence of a solar convective core and some solar-like stars – A
creator: Qian-Sheng Zhang, Jørgen Christensen-Dalsgaard, Yan Li
description: Abstract Convective-core overshoot mixing is a significant uncertainty in stellar evolution. Because numerical simulations and turbulent convection models predict exponentially decreasing radial rms turbulent velocity, a popular treatment of the overshoot mixing is to apply a diffusion process with exponentially decreasing diffusion coefficient.

title: Learning video retrieval models with relevance-aware online mining
creator: Alex Falcon, Giuseppe Serra, Oswald Lanz
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alex Falcon, Giuseppe Serra, Oswald Lanz. Due to the amount of videos and related captions uploaded every hour, deep learning-based solutions for cross-modal video retrieval are attracting more and more attention. A typical approach consists in learning a joint text-video embedding space, where the similarity of a video and its associated caption is maximized, whereas a lower similarity is enforced with all the other captions, called negatives .

title: Reconsidering the relation between “matter wave interference” and “wave-particle duality”
creator: Lukas Mairhofer, Oliver Passon
description: Abstract Interference of more and more massive objects provides a spectacular confirmation of quantum theory. It is usually regarded as support for “wave-particle duality” and in an extension of this duality even as support for “complementarity”. We first give an outline of the historical development of these notions.

title: Improved estimation for energy dissipation in biochemical oscillations
creator: Zhiyu Cao, Zhonghuai Hou
description: Abstract Biochemical oscillations, regulating the timing of life processes, need to consume energy to achieve good performance on crucial functions, such as high accuracy of phase period and high sensitivity to external signals. However, it is a great challenge to precisely estimate the energy dissipation in such systems.

title: Architectures and Synchronization Techniques for Distributed Satellite Systems: A Survey
creator: LIZ MARTINEZ MARRERO 1, JUAN C. MERLANO DUNCAN 2, JORGE QUEROL 3, SUMIT KUMAR 4, JEVGENIJ KRIVOCHIZA 5, SHREE KRISHNA SHARMA 6, SYMEON CHATZINOTAS 7, ADRIANO CAMPS 8,9, BJÖRN OTTERSTEN 10
description: Abstract CDSS is a key enabling technology for the future of remote sensing and communication missions. However, they have to meet strict synchronization requirements before their use is generalized. When clock or local oscillator signals are generated locally at each of the distributed nodes, achieving exact synchronization in absolute phase, frequency, and time is a complex problem.

title: Generalized radius problems for quotient functions having fixed second coefficient
creator: Swati Anand, Naveen Kumar Jain, Sushil Kumar
description: Abstract . In this manuscript, we deal with three classes of quotient functions having fixed second coefficient described on open unit disk. The radius of strongly starlikeness, lemniscate starlikeness, lune starlikeness, parabolic starlikeness, sine starlikeness, exponential starlikeness and several other radius estimates for such classes are examined. Relevant relations of obtained radius estimates with the existing estimates are also discussed.

title: One-step weighting to generalize and transport treatment effect estimates to a target population Thanks: We thank the Editor, Associate Editor, and two anonymous reviewers for helpful comments . We thank Eli Ben-Michael, Larry Han, Kosuke Imai, Yige Li, Bijan Niknam, Zhu Shen, and Yi Zhang for helpf
creator: Ambarish Chattopadhyay, Eric R. Cohn, José R. Zubizarreta
description: Abstract The problem of generalization and transportation of treatment effect estimates from a study sample to a target population is central to empirical research and statistical methodology. In both randomized experiments and observational studies, weighting methods are often used with this objective.

title: Engineering the speedup of quantum tunneling in Josephson systems via dissipation
creator: D. Maile, J. Ankerhold, S. Andergassen, W. Belzig, G. Rastelli
description: Abstract We theoretically investigate the escape rate occurring via quantum tunneling in a system affected by tailored dissipation. Specifically, we study the environmental assisted quantum tunneling of the superconducting phase in a current-biased Josephson junction. We consider Ohmic resistors inducing dissipation both in the phase and in the charge of the quantum circuit.

title: Analysis of a Cesium lattice optical clock
creator: A. Sharma, S. Kolkowitz, and M. Saffman
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. Sharma, S. Kolkowitz, and M. Saffman. We propose and analyze a Cesium lattice optical clock (CLOC) which has the potential for high performance and simple operation in a compact form factor using a forbidden optical transition in Cs atoms at 685 nm. Cs atoms are trapped in a 3D optical lattice using a magic trap wavelength of λ m = 803 ​ n ​ m \lambda_{\textrm{m}}=803\penalty\ \textrm{n}m .

title: Developing a Chemical and Structural Understanding of the Surface Oxide in a Niobium Superconducting Qubit
creator: Akshay A. Murthy, Paul Masih Das, Stephanie M. Ribet, Cameron Kopas, Jaeyel Lee, Matthew J. Reagor, Lin Zhou, Matthew J. Kramer, Mark C. Hersam, Mattia Checchin, Anna Grasselino, Roberto dos Reis, Vinayak P. Dravid, Alexander Romanenko, Akshay A. Murthy, ∗,† Paul Masih Das, ‡ Stephanie M. Ribet, ‡,¶
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Akshay A. Murthy, Paul Masih Das, Stephanie M. Ribet, Cameron Kopas, Jaeyel Lee, Matthew J. Reagor, Lin Zhou, Matthew J. Kramer, Mark C. Hersam, Mattia Checchin, Anna Grasselino, Roberto dos Reis, Vinayak P. Dravid, Alexander Romanenko, Akshay A. Murthy, ∗,† Paul Masih Das, ‡ Stephanie M. Ribet, ‡,¶. Superconducting thin films of niobium have been extensively employed in transmon qubit architectures. Although these architectures have demonstrated remarkable improvements in recent years, further improvements in performance through materials engineering will aid in large-scale deployment.

title: Procesi’s Conjecture on the Formanek-Weingarten Function is False Thanks: MD is supported from Narodowe Centrum Nauki , grant 2021/42/E/ST1/00162/ Thanks: JN is supported by NSF grant DMS 1812288 and a Lattimer Fellowship.
creator: Maciej Dołęga, Jonathan Novak
description: Abstract . In this paper, we disprove a recent monotonicity conjecture of C. Procesi on the generating function for monotone walks on the symmetric group, an object which is equivalent to the Weingarten function of the unitary group. 1. Introduction Let \Gamma_{d} be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group \mathrm{S}(d) as generated by the conjugacy class of transpositions.

title: —Supplementary Materials— DeciWatch: A Simple Baseline for 10 × 10\times Efficient 2D and 3D Pose Estimation
creator: Ailing Zeng 1, Xuan Ju 1, Lei Yang 2, Ruiyuan Gao 1, Xizhou Zhu 2, Bo Dai 3, Qiang Xu 1
description: Abstract In Sec. 1 , we present dataset descriptions. Next, we present results of efficient labeling in Sec. 2 and the generalization ability of DeciWatch in Sec. 4 . Then, we show more ablation studies on different sampling ratios, model designs of DenoiseNet and RecoverNet , and hyper-parameters in Sec. 5 . Moreover, we show qualitative comparison results in Sec.

title: Improved short-segment detection statistic for continuous gravitational waves
creator: P. B. Covas 1 , R. Prix 1
description: Abstract Continuous gravitational waves represent one of the long-sought types of signals that have yet to be detected. Due to their small amplitude, long observational datasets (months-years) have to be analyzed together, thereby vastly increasing the computational cost of these searches.

title: Attacking deep networks with surrogate-based adversarial black-box methods is easy
creator: Nicholas A. Lord, Romain Mueller & Luca Bertinetto
description: Abstract A recent line of work on black-box adversarial attacks has revived the use of transfer from surrogate models by integrating it into query-based search. However, we find that existing approaches of this type underperform their potential, and can be overly complicated besides.

title: Time series analysis and modelling of the freezing of gait phenomenon
creator: Ai Wang, Jan Sieber, William R. Young, Krasimira Tsaneva-Atanasova
description: Abstract Freezing of Gait (FOG) is one of the most debilitating symptoms of Parkinson’s Disease and is associated with falls and loss of independence. The patho-physiological mechanisms underpinning FOG are currently poorly understood. In this paper we combine time series analysis and mathematical modelling to study the FOG phenomenon’s dynamics.

title: Tangles and Hierarchical Clustering
creator: Eva Fluck
description: Abstract We establish a connection between tangles, a concept from structural graph theory that plays a central role in Robertson and Seymour’s graph minor project, and hierarchical clustering. Tangles cannot only be defined for graphs, but in fact for arbitrary connectivity functions, which are functions defined on the subsets of some finite universe.

title: Radical support for multigraded ideals Thanks: The first and the second authors were partially supported by PRIN 2020355B8Y “Squarefree Gröbner degenerations, special varieties and related topics” and by GNSAGA-INdAM
creator: A. Conca, E. De Negri, E. Gorla
description: Abstract . Can one tell if an ideal is radical just by looking at the degrees of the generators? In general, this is hopeless. However, there are special collections of degrees in multigraded polynomial rings, with the property that any multigraded ideal generated by elements of those degrees is radical. We call such a collection of degrees a radical support.

title: Quantum graphs: different perspectives, homomorphisms and quantum automorphisms
creator: Matthew Daws
description: Abstract We undertake a study of the notion of a quantum graph over arbitrary finite-dimensional C ∗ C^{*} -algebras B B equipped with arbitrary faithful states. Quantum graphs are realised principally as either certain operators on L 2 ​ ( B ) L^{2}(B) , the quantum adjacency matrices, or as certain operator bimodules over B ′ B^{\prime} .

title: The Second Catalog of Interplanetary Network Localizations of Konus Short Duration Gamma-Ray Bursts Facilities: Wind (Konus), Fermi (GBM and LAT), Swift (BAT and XRT), Suzaku (WAM), AGILE (MCAL), ISS (CALET-CGBM), Insight -HXMT(HE), GECAM-B, INTEGRAL (SPI-ACS), MESSENGER (GRNS), Mars-Odyssey (HEND)
creator: D. Svinkin, K. Hurley, A. Ridnaia, A. Lysenko, D. Frederiks, S. Golenetskii, A. Tsvetkova, M. Ulanov, A. Kokomov, T. L. Cline, I. Mitrofanov, D. Golovin, A. Kozyrev, M. Litvak, A. Sanin, A. Goldstein, M.S. Briggs, C. Wilson-Hodge, E. Burns, A. von Kienlin, X.-L. Zhang, A. Rau, V. Savchenko, E. Bozzo
description: Abstract We present the catalog of Interplanetary Network (IPN) localizations for 199 short-duration gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs) detected by the Konus- Wind (KW) experiment between 2011 January 1 and 2021 August 31, which extends the initial sample of IPN localized KW sGRBs ( Pal’shin et al. 2013 ) to 495 events.

title: Recovery of piecewise smooth density and Lamé parameters from high-frequency exterior Cauchy data
creator: Sombuddha Bhattacharyya, Maarten V. de Hoop, Vitaly Katsnelson, Gunther Uhlmann
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sombuddha Bhattacharyya, Maarten V. de Hoop, Vitaly Katsnelson, Gunther Uhlmann. We consider an isotropic elastic medium occupying a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ 3 \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3} whose density and Lamé parameters are piecewise smooth. In the elastic wave initial value inverse problem, we are given the solution operator for the elastic wave equation, but only outside Ω \Omega and only for initial data supported outside Ω \Omega , and we study the recovery of the density and Lamé parameters.

title: Existence of solutions to relativistic non-Abelian Chern-Simons-Higgs vortex equations on graphs Thanks: 1 School of Mathematics and Statistics, Henan University, Kaifeng, Henan 475004, P. R. China. Thanks: Emails: yuanyhu@mail.ustc.edu.cn (Y. Hu)
creator: Yuanyang Hu 1
description: Abstract . Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a connected finite graph. We study the relativistic non-Abelian Chern-Simons-Higgs vortex equations on the graph G G . We establish an existence result to the relativistic non-Abelian Chern-Simons-Higgs vortex equations. 1.

title: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance for Arbitrary Spin Values in the Rotating Wave Approximation
creator: Zhichen Liu, Sunghyun Kim, Richard A. Klemm
description: Abstract In order to probe the transitions of a nuclear spin s s from one of it substate quantum numbers m m to another substate m ′ m^{\prime} , the experimenter applies a magnetic field 𝑩 0 {\bm{B}}_{0} in some particular direction, such along 𝒛 ^ \hat{\bm{z}} , and then applies an weaker field 𝑩 1 ​ ( t )

title: Sample, Translate, Recombine: Leveraging Audio Alignments for Data Augmentation in End-to-end Speech Translation
creator: Tsz Kin Lam, Shigehiko Schamoni, Stefan Riezler
description: Abstract End-to-end speech translation relies on data that pair source-language speech inputs with corresponding translations into a target language. Such data are notoriously scarce, making synthetic data augmentation by back-translation or knowledge distillation a necessary ingredient of end-to-end training. In this paper, we present a novel approach to data augmentation that leverages audio alignments, linguistic properties, and translation.

title: Orion A’s complete 3D magnetic field morphology
creator: M. Tahani, J. Glover, W. Lupypciw, J.L. West, R. Kothes, R. Plume, S. Inutsuka, M-Y. Lee, I.A. Grenier, L.B.G. Knee, J.C. Brown, Y. Doi, T. Robishaw, M. Haverkorn
description: Abstract Magnetic fields permeate the interstellar medium and are important in the star formation process. Determining the 3D magnetic fields of molecular clouds will allow us to better understand their role in the evolution of these clouds and formation of stars.

title: Efficient conditioned face animation using frontally-viewed embedding
creator: Maxime Oquab, Daniel Haziza, Ludovic Schwartz, Tao Xu, Katayoun Zand, Rui Wang, Peirong Liu, Camille Couprie
description: Abstract As the quality of few shot facial animation from landmarks increases, new applications become possible, such as ultra low bandwidth video chat compression with a high degree of realism. However, there are some important challenges to tackle in order to improve the experience in real world conditions.

title: Cosmo-Paleontology: Statistics of Fossil Groups in a Gravity-Only Simulation ⋆ Corresponding author: acossairt@anl.gov
creator: Aurora Cossairt 1,⋆, Michael Buehlmann 1, Eve Kovacs 1, Xin Liu 1,2, Salman Habib 1,3, Katrin Heitmann 1
description: Abstract We present a detailed study of fossil group candidates identified in “Last Journey”, a gravity-only cosmological simulation covering a ( 3.4 ​ h − 1 ​ Gpc ) 3 \smash{(3.4\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Gpc})^{3}} volume with a particle mass resolution of m p ≈ 2.7 × 10 9 \smash{m_{p}\approx 2.7\times 10^{9}} h − 1 ​ M ⊙ \smash{h^{-1}}\mathrm{M}_{\odot} .

title: Room temperature donor incorporation for quantum devices: arsine on germanium
creator: Emily V. S. Hofmann, Taylor J. Z. Stock, Oliver Warschkow, Rebecca Conybeare, Neil J. Curson, Steven R. Schofield
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emily V. S. Hofmann, Taylor J. Z. Stock, Oliver Warschkow, Rebecca Conybeare, Neil J. Curson, Steven R. Schofield. Germanium has emerged as an exceptionally promising material for spintronics and quantum information applications, with significant fundamental advantages over silicon. However, efforts to create atomic-scale devices using donor atoms as qubits have largely focussed on phosphorus in silicon.

title: Periodic traveling waves in a taut cable on a bilinear elastic substrate
creator: Lucio Demeio
description: Abstract The wave propagation problem on a taut cable resting on a bilinear substrate is investigated, without and with a distribute transversal load. The piecewise nature of the problem offers a sufficiently simple kind of nonlinearity as to permit a closed form solution both for the wave phase velocity and the wave form.

title: Object discovery and representation networks
creator: Olivier J. Hénaff, Skanda Koppula, Evan Shelhamer, Daniel Zoran, Andrew Jaegle, Andrew Zisserman, João Carreira, Relja Arandjelović
description: Abstract The promise of self-supervised learning (SSL) is to leverage large amounts of unlabeled data to solve complex tasks. While there has been excellent progress with simple, image-level learning, recent methods have shown the advantage of including knowledge of image structure.

title: Dynamics simulation and numerical analysis of arbitrary time-dependent 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{PT} -symmetric system based on density operators
creator: Xiaogang Li, Chao Zheng, Jiancun Gao, Guilu Long
description: Abstract 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{PT} -symmetric system has attracted extensive attention in recent years because of its unique properties and applications. How to simulate 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{PT} -symmetric system in traditional quantum mechanical system has not only fundamental theoretical significance but also practical value.

title: GLASS : A Citizen-Centric Distributed Data-Sharing Model within an E-Governance Architecture
creator: Owen Lo, William J. Buchanan, Sarwar Sayeed *, Pavlos Papadopoulos, Nikolaos Pitropakis * and Christos Chrysoulas
description: Abstract E-governance is a process that aims to enhance a government’s ability to simplify all the processes that may involve government, citizens, businesses, and so on. The rapid evolution of digital technologies has often created the necessity for the establishment of an e-Governance model.

title: PosePipe: Open-Source Human Pose Estimation Pipeline for Clinical Research
creator: R. James Cotton
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by R. James Cotton. There has been significant progress in machine learning algorithms for human pose estimation that may provide immense value in rehabilitation and movement sciences. However, there remain several challenges to routine use of these tools for clinical practice and translational research, including: 1) high technical barrier to entry, 2) rapidly evolving space of algorithms, 3) challenging algorithmic interdependencies, and 4) complex data management requirements between these components.

title: 1 S 0 Pairing Gaps, Chemical Potentials and Entrainment Matrix in Superfluid Neutron-Star Cores for the Brussels–Montreal Functionals
creator: Valentin Allard, Nicolas Chamel *
description: Abstract Temperature and velocity-dependent 1 S 0 pairing gaps, chemical potentials and entrainment matrix in dense homogeneous neutron–proton superfluid mixtures constituting the outer core of neutron stars, are determined fully self-consistently by solving numerically the time-dependent Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov equations over the whole range of temperatures and flow velocities for which superfluidity can exist.

title: Double sweep LU decomposition for American options under negative rates
creator: Fabien Le Floc’h
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fabien Le Floc’h. The classic Brennan-Schwartz algorithm to solve the linear complementary problem, which arises from the finite difference discretization of the partial differential equation related to American option pricing does not lead to the exact solution under negative interest rates. This is due to the two exercise boundaries which may appear under negative interest rate, while the algorithm was proven to lead to the exact solution in the case of a single exercise boundary only.

title: Analysis of a Gray-Box Operator for Vertex Cover
creator: Samuel Baguley, Tobias Friedrich, Timo Kötzing, Xiaoyue Li, Marcus Pappik, Ziena Zeif
description: Abstract Combinatorial optimization problems are a prominent application area of evolutionary algorithms, where the (1+1) EA is one of the most investigated. We extend this algorithm by introducing some problem knowledge with a specialized mutation operator which works under the assumption that the number of 1s of a solution is critical, as frequently happens in combinatorial optimization.

title: On integral mixed Cayley graphs over non-abelian finite groups admitting an abelian subgroup of index 2
creator: Angelot Behajaina, François Legrand
description: Abstract . Recently, several works by a number of authors have provided characterizations of integral undirected Cayley graphs over generalized dihedral groups and generalized dicyclic groups. We generalize and unify these results in two different ways. Firstly, we work over arbitrary non-abelian finite groups admitting an abelian subgroup of index 2.

title: Quantum computing for data analysis in high energy physics
creator: Andrea Delgado, Kathleen E. Hamilton, Prasanna Date, Jean-Roch Vlimant, Duarte Magano, Yasser Omar, Pedrame Bargassa, Alessio Gianelle, Lorenzo Sestini, Donatella Lucchesi, Davide Zuliani, Davide Nicotra, Jacco de Vries, Domenica Dibenedetto, Miriam Lucio Martinez, Eduardo Rodrigues, Carlos Vazquez
description: Abstract Some of the biggest achievements of the modern era of particle physics, such as the discovery of the Higgs boson, have been made possible by the tremendous effort in building and operating large-scale experiments like the Large Hadron Collider or the Tevatron.

title: Submitted to the Proceedings of the US Community Study
creator: on the Future of Particle Physics (Snowmass 2021)
description: Abstract August 8, 2026 Analysis Cyberinfrastructure: Challenges and Opportunities K. Lannon, P. Brenner, M. Hildreth, K. Hurtado Anampa, A. Malta Rodrigues, K. Mohrman, D. Thain, B. Tovar University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame, IN 46556, USA ABSTRACT Analysis cyberinfrastructure refers to the combination of software and computer hardware used to support late-stage data analysis in High Energy Physics (HEP).

title: Neural-Network-Directed Genetic Programmer for Discovery of Governing Equations
creator: Shahab Razavi, Eric R. Gamazon
description: Abstract We develop a symbolic regression framework for extracting the governing mathematical expressions from observed data. The evolutionary approach, faiGP, is designed to leverage the properties of a function algebra that have been encoded into a grammar, providing a theoretical guarantee of universal approximation and a way to minimize bloat.

title: DePS: An improved deep learning model for de novo peptide sequencing
creator: Cheng Ge, Yi Lu, Jia Qu, Liangxu Xie, Feng Wang, Hong Zhang, Ren Kong, Shan Chang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Cheng Ge, Yi Lu, Jia Qu, Liangxu Xie, Feng Wang, Hong Zhang, Ren Kong, Shan Chang. De novo peptide sequencing from mass spectrometry data is an important method for protein identification. Recently, various deep learning approaches were applied for de novo peptide sequencing and DeepNovoV2 is one of the represetative models.

title: Hierarchical Clustering and Matrix Completion for the Reconstruction of World Input-Output Tables Journal: AStA Advances in Statistical Analysis
creator: Rodolfo Metulini, Giorgio Gnecco, Francesco Biancalani, Massimo Riccaboni
description: Abstract World Input-Output (I/O) matrices provide the networks of within- and cross-country economic relations. In the context of I/O analysis, the methodology adopted by national statistical offices in data collection raises the issue of obtaining reliable data in a timely fashion and it makes the reconstruction of (part of) the I/O matrices of particular interest.

title: Understanding robustness and generalization of artificial neural networks through Fourier masks. fabio.anselmi@bcm.edu, anselmi@mit.edu, nikos.karantzas@bcm.edu
creator: Nikos Karantzas, Emma Besier, Josue Ortega Caro, Xaq Pitkow, Andreas S. Tolias, Ankit B. Patel, Fabio Anselmi
description: Abstract Despite the enormous success of artificial neural networks (ANNs) in many disciplines, the characterization of their computations and the origin of key properties such as generalization and robustness remain open questions. Recent literature suggests that robust networks with good generalization properties tend to be biased towards processing low frequencies in images.

title: QUBOs for Sorting Lists and Building Trees
creator: Christian Bauckhage, Thore Gerlach, Nico Piatkowski
description: Abstract We show that the fundamental tasks of sorting lists and building search trees or heaps can be modeled as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problems (QUBOs). The idea is to understand these tasks as permutation problems and to devise QUBOs whose solutions represent appropriate permutation matrices.

title: Near-Zone Symmetries of Kerr Black Holes
creator: Lam Hui, Austin Joyce, Riccardo Penco, Luca Santoni, Adam R. Solomon
description: Abstract We study the near-zone symmetries of a massless scalar field on four-dimensional black hole backgrounds. We provide a geometric understanding that unifies various recently discovered symmetries as part of an SO ⁡ ( 4 , 2 ) {\rm SO}(4,2) group.

title: Robust quantum many-body scars in lattice gauge theories
creator: Jad C. Halimeh, Luca Barbiero, Philipp Hauke, Fabian Grusdt, Annabelle Bohrdt
description: Abstract Quantum many-body scarring is a paradigm of weak ergodicity breaking arising due to the presence of special nonthermal many-body eigenstates that possess low entanglement entropy, are equally spaced in energy, and concentrate in certain parts of the Hilbert space.

title: The Compact Structures of Massive z ∼ 0.7 z\sim 0.7 Post-Starburst Galaxies in the SQuIGG L → \vec{L} E Sample Journal: ApJ
creator: David J. Setton, Margaret Verrico, Rachel Bezanson, Jenny E. Greene, Katherine A. Suess, Andy D. Goulding, Justin S. Spilker, Mariska Kriek, Robert Feldmann, Desika Narayanan, Khalil Hall-Hooper, Erin Kado-Fong
description: Abstract We present structural measurements of 145 spectroscopically selected intermediate-redshift (z ∼ \sim 0.7), massive ( M ⋆ ∼ 10 11 ​ M ⊙ M_{\star}\sim 10^{11}\ M_{\odot} ) post-starburst galaxies from the SQuIGG L → \vec{L} E Sample measured using wide-depth Hyper Suprime-Cam i-band imaging.

title: Bayesian field-level inference of primordial non-Gaussianity using next-generation galaxy surveys 2022 Bayesian field-level inference of primordial non-Gaussianity using next-generation galaxy surveys – 16
creator: Adam Andrews, Jens Jasche, Guilhem Lavaux, Fabian Schmidt
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Adam Andrews, Jens Jasche, Guilhem Lavaux, Fabian Schmidt. Detecting and measuring a non-Gaussian signature of primordial origin in the density field is a major science goal of next-generation galaxy surveys. The signal will permit us to determine primordial physics processes and constrain models of cosmic inflation. While traditional approaches utilise a limited set of statistical summaries of the galaxy distribution to constrain primordial non-Gaussianity, we present a field-level approach by Bayesian forward-modelling the entire three-dimensional galaxy survey.

title: Stability Analysis of a Non-Unitary CFT
creator: Masataka Watanabe
description: Abstract We study instability of the lowest dimension operator ( i.e., the imaginary part of its operator dimension) in the rank- Q Q traceless symmetric representation of the O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) Wilson-Fisher fixed point in D = 4 + ϵ D=4+\epsilon .

title: Pre-Trained Multilingual Sequence-to-Sequence Models: A Hope for Low-Resource Language Translation?
creator: En-Shiun Annie Lee , Sarubi Thillainathan , Shravan Nayak , Surangika Ranathunga ,, David Ifeoluwa Adelani , Ruisi Su ,, Arya D. McCarthy
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by En-Shiun Annie Lee , Sarubi Thillainathan , Shravan Nayak , Surangika Ranathunga ,, David Ifeoluwa Adelani , Ruisi Su ,, Arya D. McCarthy. What can pre-trained multilingual sequence-to-sequence models like mBART contribute to translating low-resource languages? We conduct a thorough empirical experiment in 10 languages to ascertain this, considering five factors: (1) the amount of fine-tuning data, (2) the noise in the fine-tuning data, (3) the amount of pre-training data in the model, (4) the impact of domain mismatch, and (5) language typology.

title: Tidally-induced nonlinear resonances in EMRIs with an analogue model
creator: David Bronicki, Alejandro Cárdenas-Avendaño, Leo C. Stein
description: Abstract One of the important targets for the future space-based gravitational wave observatory LISA is extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs), where long and accurate waveform modeling is necessary for detection and characterization. Modeling EMRI dynamics requires accounting for effects such as the ones induced by an external tidal field, which can break integrability at resonances and cause significant dephasing.

title: Limits to gauge coupling in the dark sector set by the non-observation of instanton- induced decay of Super-Heavy Dark Matter in the Pierre Auger Observatory data
creator: P. Abreu, M. Aglietta, J.M. Albury, I. Allekotte, K. Almeida Cheminant, A. Almela, R. Aloisio, J. Alvarez-Muñiz, R. Alves Batista, J. Ammerman Yebra, G.A. Anastasi, L. Anchordoqui, B. Andrada, S. Andringa, C. Aramo, P.R. Araújo Ferreira, E. Arnone, J. C. Arteaga Velázquez, H. Asorey, P. Assis, G. Av
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by P. Abreu, M. Aglietta, J.M. Albury, I. Allekotte, K. Almeida Cheminant, A. Almela, R. Aloisio, J. Alvarez-Muñiz, R. Alves Batista, J. Ammerman Yebra, G.A. Anastasi, L. Anchordoqui, B. Andrada, S. Andringa, C. Aramo, P.R. Araújo Ferreira, E. Arnone, J. C. Arteaga Velázquez, H. Asorey, P. Assis, G. Av. Instantons, which are non-perturbative solutions to Yang-Mills equations, provide a signal for the occurrence of quantum tunneling between distinct classes of vacua. They can give rise to decays of particles otherwise forbidden.

title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics and Wormholes
description: Abstract We show that a recent reformulation of hydrodynamic equations for a large class of models consisting of q-dits on a graph with short range interactions is sufficient for understanding chaotic behavior. Any such system consists of large subsystems coupled together by interactions whose relative strength goes to zero with the subsystem size.

title: Evidence of surface heterogeneity on active asteroid (3200) Phaethon Journal: Icarus
creator: Eric MacLennan, Sean Marshall, Mikael Granvik
description: Abstract Thermal infrared emission and thermophysical modeling techniques are powerful tools in deciphering the surface properties of asteroids. The near-Earth asteroid (3200) Phaethon is an active asteroid with a very small perihelion distance and is likely the source of the Geminid meteor shower.

title: Convergence of optimal expected utility for a sequence of discrete-time markets in initially enlarged filtrations
creator: Geoff Lindsell
description: Abstract In this paper, we extend Kreps’ conjecture that optimal expected utility in the classic Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) economy is the limit of optimal expected utility for a sequence of discrete-time economies in initially enlarged filtrations converge to the BSM economy in an initially enlarged filtration in a ”strong” sense.

title: Non-minimal non-Abelian quantum vector fields in curved spacetime
creator: L. L. Salcedo
description: Abstract The quantum effective action of non-minimal vector fields with Abelian or non-Abelian gauge degrees of freedom in curved spacetime is studied. The Proca or Yang-Mills fields are coupled to a local mass-like term acting in both coordinate and gauge spaces.

title: 𝐬𝐢𝐧 𝟐 ⁡ 𝜽 𝑾 \sin^{2}\theta_{W} and neutrino electromagnetic interactions in CE 𝝂 ¯ 𝒆 \overline{\nu}_{e} NS with different quenching factors
creator: Amir N. Khan
description: Abstract Recently, evidence for the observation of about 2 keV and below nuclear recoils from the coherent scattering of reactor anti-neutrinos off the germanium nuclei has been reported. We analyze the observed data to estimate the value of the weak mixing angle and constrain the neutrino millicharge, magnetic moment, charge radius and anapole moment contributing to the coherent scattering process.

title: A Simple and Computationally Trivial Estimator for Grouped Fixed Effects Models An earlier version of this paper based on the third chapter of my Ph.D. dissertation at CREST was circulated under the title “Make the Difference! Computationally Trivial Estimators for Grouped Fixed Effects Models”. I t
creator: Martin Mugnier
description: Abstract This paper introduces a new fixed effects estimator for linear panel data models with clustered time patterns of unobserved heterogeneity. The method avoids non-convex and combinatorial optimization by combining a preliminary consistent estimator of the slope coefficient, an agglomerative pairwise-differencing clustering of cross-sectional units, and a pooled ordinary least squares regression.

title: Gate-Shift-Fuse for Video Action Recognition
creator: Swathikiran Sudhakaran, Sergio Escalera, and Oswald Lanz
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Swathikiran Sudhakaran, Sergio Escalera, and Oswald Lanz. Convolutional Neural Networks are the de facto models for image recognition. However 3D CNNs, the straight forward extension of 2D CNNs for video recognition, have not achieved the same success on standard action recognition benchmarks. One of the main reasons for this reduced performance of 3D CNNs is the increased computational complexity requiring large scale annotated datasets to train them in scale. 3D kernel factorization approaches have been proposed to reduce the complexity of 3D CNNs.

title: Neural network processing of holographic images
description: Abstract HOLODEC, an airborne cloud particle imager, captures holographic images of a fixed volume of cloud to characterize the types and sizes of cloud particles, such as water droplets and ice crystals. Cloud particle properties include position, diameter, and shape.

title: Sat-NeRF: Learning Multi-View Satellite Photogrammetry With Transient Objects and Shadow Modeling Using RPC Cameras
creator: Roger Marí, Gabriele Facciolo, Thibaud Ehret
description: Abstract We introduce the Satellite Neural Radiance Field (Sat-NeRF), a new end-to-end model for learning multi-view satellite photogrammetry in the wild. Sat-NeRF combines some of the latest trends in neural rendering with native satellite camera models, represented by rational polynomial coefficient (RPC) functions.

title: Optothermal evolution of active colloidal matter in defocused laser trap
creator: Diptabrata Paul, Rahul Chand, G V Pavan Kumar
description: Abstract Optothermal interaction of active colloidal matter can facilitate environmental cues which can influence the dynamics of active soft matter systems. The optically induced thermal effect can be harnessed to study non-equilibrium thermodynamics as well as applied to self-propel colloids and form assemblies. In this work, we employ a defocused laser trap to form self-evolving colloidal active matter.

title: Price Tracing: Linking Nodal Prices in Optimized Power Systems
creator: Fabian Hofmann, Markus Schlott
description: Abstract Optimizing the total cost of power systems is a common tool for network operation and planning. Besides valuable information about how to run and possibly expand a power system, the optimization provides an optimal Locational Marginal Price per node and time step.

title: Orca : A Network and Architecture Co-design for Offloading μ ​ s \mu s -scale Datacenter Applications
creator: Yifan Yuan 1 , Jinghan Huang 1 ,Yan Sun 1 , Tianchen Wang 1 , Jacob Nelson 2 , Dan R. K. Ports 2 , Yipeng Wang 3 , Ren Wang 3 , Charlie Tai 3 , Nam Sung Kim 1
description: Abstract 1 1 1 This work has been accepted by a conference. The authoritative version of this work “RAMBDA: RDMA-driven Acceleration Framework for Memory-intensive us-scale Datacenter Applications” will appear in the Proceedings of the 48th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on High-Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA-29), 2023.

title: Observational constraints on the interacting dark energy - dark matter (IDM) cosmological models Journal: Physics of The Dark Universe
creator: T. Harko, K. Asadi, H. Moshafi, H. Sheikhahmadi
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by T. Harko, K. Asadi, H. Moshafi, H. Sheikhahmadi. Particle creation (or annihilation) mechanisms, described by either quantum field theoretical models, or by the thermodynamics of irreversible processes, play an important role in the evolution of the early Universe, like, for example, in the warm inflationary scenario.

title: Memorizing Transformers
creator: Yuhuai Wu, Markus N. Rabe, DeLesley Hutchins, Christian Szegedy {yuhuai,mrabe,delesley,szegedy}@google.com
description: Abstract Language models typically need to be trained or finetuned in order to acquire new knowledge, which involves updating their weights. We instead envision language models that can simply read and memorize new data at inference time, thus acquiring new knowledge immediately. In this work, we extend language models with the ability to memorize the internal representations of past inputs.

title: Complex Analytic Dependence on the Dielectric Permittivity in ENZ Materials: The Photonic Doping Example
creator: Robert V. Kohn and Raghavendra Venkatraman
description: Abstract . Motivated by the physics literature on “photonic doping” of scatterers made from “epsilon-near-zero” (ENZ) materials, we consider how the scattering of time-harmonic TM electromagnetic waves by a cylindrical ENZ region Ω × ℝ \Omega\times\mathbb{R} is affected by the presence of a “dopant” D ⊂ Ω D\subset\Omega in which the dielectric permittivity is not near zero.

title: Persistent revivals in a system of trapped bosonic atoms
creator: Carlos Diaz Mejia, Javier de la Cruz, Sergio Lerma-Hernández, Jorge G. Hirsch
description: Abstract Dynamical signatures of quantum chaos are observed in the survival probability of different initial states, in a system of cold atoms trapped in a linear chain with site noise and open boundary conditions. It is shown that chaos is present in the region of small disorder, at intermediate energies.

title: Creating Multimedia Summaries Using Tweets and Videos
creator: Anietie Andy, Siyi Liu, Daphne Ippolito, Reno Kriz, Chris Callison-Burch, Derry Wijaya
description: Abstract While popular televised events such as presidential debates or TV shows are airing, people provide commentary on them in real-time. In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective approach to combine social media commentary and videos to create a multimedia summary of televised events.

title: ℓ p \ell_{p} Slack Norm Support Vector Data Description
creator: Shervin Rahimzadeh Arashloo
description: Abstract The support vector data description (SVDD) approach serves as a de facto standard for one-class classification where the learning task entails inferring the smallest hyper-sphere to enclose target objects while linearly penalising any errors/slacks via an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -norm penalty term.

title: Risk-Averse No-Regret Learning in Online Convex Games
creator: Zifan Wang, Yi Shen, Michael M. Zavlanos
description: Abstract We consider an online stochastic game with risk-averse agents whose goal is to learn optimal decisions that minimize the risk of incurring significantly high costs. Specifically, we use the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) as a risk measure that the agents can estimate using bandit feedback in the form of the cost values of only their selected actions.

title: Prospects for reconstructing the gravitational-wave signals from core-collapse supernovae with Advanced LIGO-Virgo and the BayesWave algorithm
creator: Nayyer Raza, Jess McIver, Gergely Dálya, Peter Raffai
description: Abstract Our current understanding of the core-collapse supernova explosion mechanism is incomplete, with multiple viable models for how the initial shock wave might be energized enough to lead to a successful explosion. Detection of a gravitational-wave signal emitted in the initial few seconds after stellar core-collapse would provide unique and crucial insight into this process.

title: A 5% measurement of the Hubble-Lemaître constant from Type II supernovae 2022 A 5% measurement of the Hubble-Lemaître constant from Type II supernovae – References
creator: T. de Jaeger, L. Galbany A. G. Riess, B. E. Stahl, B. J. Shappee, A. V. Filippenko, W. Zheng
description: Abstract The most stringent local measurement of the Hubble-Lemaître constant from Cepheid-calibrated Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) differs from the value inferred via the cosmic microwave background radiation ( Planck + Λ +\Lambda CDM) by ∼ 5 ​ σ \sim 5\sigma .

title: Speaker Information Can Guide Models to Better Inductive Biases: A Case Study On Predicting Code-Switching
creator: Alissa Ostapenko, Shuly Wintner, Melinda Fricke, Yulia Tsvetkov
description: Abstract Natural language processing (NLP) models trained on people-generated data can be unreliable because, without any constraints, they can learn from spurious correlations that are not relevant to the task. We hypothesize that enriching models with speaker information in a controlled, educated way can guide them to pick up on relevant inductive biases.

title: On Distributed Gravitational N N -Body Simulations
creator: Alexander Brandt
description: Abstract The N N -body problem is a classic problem involving a system of N N discrete bodies mutually interacting in a dynamical system. At any moment in time there are N ⁡ ( N − 1 ) / 2 {N(N-1)}/{2} such interactions occurring.

title: Integer partitions with large Dyson rank
creator: Colin Albert, Olivia Beckwith, Irfan Demetoglu, Robert Dicks, John H. Smith, Jasmine Wang
description: Abstract . The Dyson rank of an integer partition is the difference between its largest part and the number of parts it contains. Using Fine-Dyson symmetry, we study counts of partitions whose rank lies in fixed residue classes and has large absolute value. We prove formulas relating these counts for partitions of different sizes. August 8, 2026 1.

title: One-Bit Phase Retrieval: More Samples Means Less Complexity? Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Science Foundation Grant CCF-1704401. Thanks: A. Eamaz, F. Yeganegi and M. Soltanalian are with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Illinois Chicago,
creator: Arian Eamaz, Farhang Yeganegi, and
description: Abstract The classical problem of phase retrieval has found a wide array of applications in optics, imaging and signal processing. In this paper, we consider the phase retrieval problem in a one-bit setting, where the signals are sampled using one-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADCs).

title: On the Usefulness of the Fit-on-the-Test View on Evaluating Calibration of Classifiers
creator: Markus Kängsepp, Kaspar Valk, Meelis Kull
description: Abstract Every uncalibrated classifier has a corresponding true calibration map that calibrates its confidence. Deviations of this idealistic map from the identity map reveal miscalibration. Such calibration errors can be reduced with many post-hoc calibration methods which fit some family of calibration maps on a validation dataset.

title: Time domain methods for X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy
creator: Eric D. Feigelson, Vinay L. Kashyap and Aneta Siemiginowska
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eric D. Feigelson, Vinay L. Kashyap and Aneta Siemiginowska. A variety of statistical methods for understanding variability in the time domain for low count rate X-ray and gamma-ray sources are explored. Variability can be detected using nonparametric (Anderson-Darling and overdispersion tests) and parametric (sequential likelihood-based tests) tools. Once detected, variability can be characterized by nonparametric (autocorrelation function, structure function, wavelet analysis) and parametric (multiple change point model such as Bayesian Blocks, integer autoregressive models, C-statistic and Poisson regression) methods.

title: Neutron star mass formula with nuclear saturation parameters
creator: Hajime Sotani, Hajime Togashi
description: Abstract We derive the empirical formulas for the neutron star mass and gravitational redshift as a function of the central density and specific combination of the nuclear saturation parameters, which are applicable to the stellar models constructed with the central density up to threefold nuclear saturation density. Combining the both empirical formulas, one also estimates the neutron star radius.

title: Stochastic Simulation Uncertainty Analysis to Accelerate Flexible Biomanufacturing Process Development
creator: Wei Xie, Russell R. Barton, Barry L. Nelson, Keqi Wang
description: Abstract Motivated by critical challenges and needs from biopharmaceuticals manufacturing, we propose a general metamodel-assisted stochastic simulation uncertainty analysis framework to accelerate the development of a simulation model with modular design for flexible production processes. There are often very limited process observations. Thus, there exist both simulation and model uncertainties in the system performance estimates.

title: Natural Language Communication with a Conversational Teachable Agent
creator: Rachel Love, Edith Law, Philip R. Cohen, Dana Kulić
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rachel Love, Edith Law, Philip R. Cohen, Dana Kulić. Conversational teachable agents offer a promising platform to support learning, both in the classroom and in remote settings. In this context, the agent takes the role of the novice, while the student takes on the role of teacher. This framing is significant for its ability to elicit the Protégé effect in the student-teacher, a pedagogical phenomenon known to increase engagement in the teaching task, and also improve cognitive outcomes.

title: Example-Based Vulnerability Detection and Repair in Java Code DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: The 30th International Conference on Program Comprehension; May 21–22, 2022; Pittsburgh, PA, USA Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 Conference: 30th International Conference on Program Comp
creator: Ying Zhang, Ya Xiao, Md Mahir Asef Kabir, Danfeng (Daphne) Yao, Na Meng
description: Abstract . The Java libraries JCA and JSSE offer cryptographic APIs to facilitate secure coding. When developers misuse some of the APIs, their code becomes vulnerable to cyber-attacks. To eliminate such vulnerabilities, people built tools to detect security-API misuses via pattern matching. However, most tools do not (1) fix misuses or (2) allow users to extend tools’ pattern sets.

title: Exponential asymptotics for elastic and elastic-gravity waves on flow past submerged obstacles
creator: Christopher J. Lustri
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christopher J. Lustri. Linearized flow past a submerged obstacle with an elastic sheet resting on the flow surface are studied in the limit that the bending length is small compared to the obstacle depth , in two and three dimensions. Gravitational effects are included in the two-dimensional geometry, but absent in the three-dimensional geometry; the Froude number is chosen so that gravitational and elastic restoring forces are comparable in size .

title: Sub-Terahertz Wireless Coverage Analysis at 142 GHz in Urban Microcell This research is supported by the NYU WIRELESS Industrial Affiliates Program and National Science Foundation (NSF) Research Grants: 1909206 and 2037845.
creator: Yunchou Xing, Ojas Kanhere, Shihao Ju, and Theodore S. Rappaport
description: Abstract Small-cell cellular base stations are going to be used for mmWave and sub-THz communication systems to provide multi-Gbps data rates and reliable coverage to mobile users. This paper analyzes the base station coverage of sub-THz communication systems and the system performance in terms of spectral efficiency through Monte Carlo simulations for both single-cell and multi-cell cases.

title: Robust Control Approaches for Minimizing the Bandwidth Ratio in Multi-Loop Control Thanks: I am thankful to Prof. Samuel Burden for his insightful discussions and suggestions. creator: Rahul Mallik
description: Abstract Conventional dc-dc, dc-ac converter control entail an inner current and outer voltage (ICOV) control loop. Stability of multi-loop control is achieved by ensuring faster dynamics of inner loops, often separating the bandwidths by large factors. Heuristically a factor-of-ten has often been used to separate the bandwidths of two adjacent loops in the nested architecture.

title: Phased Flight Trajectory Prediction with Deep Learning DOI: xxxx Journal: TIST Volume: 1 1 1 1 CCS: Information systems Data mining CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
creator: Kai Zhang, Bowen Chen
description: Abstract . The unprecedented increase of commercial airlines and private jets over the next ten years presents a challenge for air traffic control. Precise flight trajectory prediction is of great significance in air transportation management, which contributes to the decision-making for safe and orderly flights.

title: Global Well-posedness and Regularity of Weak Solutions to the Prandtl’s System Thanks: Institute of Mathematics, Academy of Mathematics and System Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100080, China. description: Abstract Abstract We continue our study on the global solution to the two-dimensional Prandtl’s system for unsteady boundary layers in the class considered by Oleinik provided that the pressure is favorable. First, by using a different method from [13], we gave a direct proof of existence of a global weak solution by a direct BV estimate.

title: Kan Extensions in Data Science and Machine Learning Conference: …; …; … …
creator: Dan Shiebler
description: Abstract . A common problem in data science is “use this function defined over this small set to generate predictions over that larger set.” Extrapolation, interpolation, statistical inference and forecasting all reduce to this problem. The Kan extension is a powerful tool in category theory that generalizes this notion.

title: Anticollinear order and degeneracy lifting in square lattice antiferromagnet LaSrCrO 4
creator: Jing Zhou, Guy Quirion, Jeffrey A. Quilliam, Huibo Cao, Feng Ye, Matthew B. Stone, Qing Huang, Haidong Zhou, Jinguang Cheng, Xiaojian Bai, Martin Mourigal, Yuan Wan, Zhiling Dun
description: Abstract We report the static and dynamic magnetic properties of LaSrCrO 4 , a seemingly canonical spin-3/2 square-lattice antiferromagnet that exhibits frustration between magnetic layers – owing to their AB stacking – and offers a rare testbed to investigate accidental-degeneracy lifting in magnetism.

title: A categorification of the Lusztig–Vogan module
creator: Scott Larson and Anna Romanov
description: Abstract . We construct two categorifications of the Lusztig–Vogan module associated to a real reductive algebraic group. The first categorification is given by semisimple complexes in an equivariant derived category, and the second is constructed as a module category over Soergel bimodules. Our categorifications are related by taking equivariant hypercohomology. 1. Introduction 1.1.

description: Abstract The Ginibre point process is given by the eigenvalue distribution of a non-hermitian complex Gaussian matrix in the infinite matrix-size limit. This is a determinantal point process (DPP) on the complex plane ℂ {\mathbb{C}} in the sense that all correlation functions are given by determinants specified by an integral kernel called the correlation kernel.

description: Abstract . We present the existence of the group inverse and its representation for the block operator matrix ( E I F 0 ) \left(\begin{array}[]{cc}E&I\\ F&0\end{array}\right) under the condition F ​ E ​ F π = 0 FEF^{\pi}=0 . The group inverse for the anti-triangular block matrices with two identical subblocks under the same condition is thereby investigated.

creator: Anan Bari Sarkar, Sougata Mardanya, Shin-Ming Huang, Barun Ghosh, Cheng-Yi Huang, Hsin Lin, Arun Bansil, Tay-Rong Chang, Amit Agarwal, Bahadur Singh
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Anan Bari Sarkar, Sougata Mardanya, Shin-Ming Huang, Barun Ghosh, Cheng-Yi Huang, Hsin Lin, Arun Bansil, Tay-Rong Chang, Amit Agarwal, Bahadur Singh. Recent classification efforts encompassing crystalline symmetries have revealed rich possibilities for solid-state systems to support a tapestry of exotic topological states. However, finding materials that realize such states remains a daunting challenge.

title: deepNIR: Datasets for generating synthetic NIR images and improved fruit detection system using deep learning techniques
creator: Inkyu Sa *, JongYoon Lim, Ho Seok Ahn, Bruce MacDonald
description: Abstract This paper presents datasets utilised for synthetic near-infrared (NIR) image generation and bounding-box level fruit detection systems. A high-quality dataset is one of the essential building blocks that can lead to success in model generalisation and the deployment of data-driven deep neural networks. In particular, synthetic data generation tasks often require more training samples than other supervised approaches.

creator: Woocheol Choi, Jimyeong Kim (Sungkyunkwan University, Mathematics)
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Woocheol Choi, Jimyeong Kim (Sungkyunkwan University, Mathematics).
