In particular, the package can handle systems with contacts that are described by complementarity constraints and provides a general framework for specifying obstacle avoidance constraints.

title: Scaling properties of background- and chiral-magnetically-driven charge separation in heavy ion collisions at s NN = 200 \sqrt{s}_{\mathrm{NN}}=200 GeV
creator: Roy A. Lacey, Niseem Magdy, Petr Parfenov, Arkadiy Taranenko
description: Abstract The Anomalous Viscous Fluid Dynamics model, AVFD, is used in concert with the charge-sensitive correlator R Ψ 2 ​ ( Δ ​ S ) R_{\Psi_{2}}(\Delta S) to investigate the scaling properties of background- and chiral-magnetically-driven (CME) charge separation ( Δ ​ S \Delta S ), characterized by the inverse variance σ R Ψ 2 − 2 \mathrm{\sigma^{-2}_{R_{\Psi_{2}}}} of the

title: Skill-based Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning of Industrial Robot Tasks with Planning and Knowledge Integration
creator: Matthias Mayr, Faseeh Ahmad, Konstantinos Chatzilygeroudis, Luigi Nardi, Volker Krueger
description: Abstract In modern industrial settings with small batch sizes it should be easy to set up a robot system for a new task. Strategies exist, e.g. the use of skills, but when it comes to handling forces and torques, these systems often fall short.

title: Multi-input segmentation of damaged brain in acute ischemic stroke patients using slow fusion with skip connection
creator: Luca Tomasetti, Mahdieh Khanmohammadi, Kjersti Engan, Liv Jorunn Høllesli, Kathinka Dæhli Kurz
description: Abstract Time is a fundamental factor during stroke treatments. A fast, automatic approach that segments the ischemic regions helps treatment decisions. In clinical use today, a set of color-coded parametric maps generated from computed tomography perfusion (CTP) images are investigated manually to decide a treatment plan.

title: Second-order optimality conditions for general nonconvex optimization problems and variational analysis of disjunctive systems
creator: Matúš Benko, Helmut Gfrerer, Jane J. Ye, Jin Zhang, Jinchuan Zhou
description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we propose second-order sufficient optimality conditions for a very general nonconvex constrained optimization problem, which covers many prominent mathematical programs. Unlike the existing results in the literature, our conditions prove to be sufficient, for an essential local minimizer of second order, under merely basic smoothness and closedness assumptions on the data defining the problem.

title: On the Generalization Mystery in Deep Learning
creator: Satrajit Chatterjee and Piotr Zielinski
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Satrajit Chatterjee and Piotr Zielinski. The generalization mystery in deep learning is the following: Why do over-parameterized neural networks trained with gradient descent (GD) generalize well on real datasets even though they are capable of fitting random datasets of comparable size? Furthermore, from among all solutions that fit the training data, how does GD find one that generalizes well (when such a well-generalizing solution exists)?

title: Risk-Sensitive Bayesian Games for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning under Policy Uncertainty Conference: Proc. of the 21st International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2022); May 9–13, 2022; Auckland, New Zealand ???
creator: Hannes Eriksson, Debabrota Basu, Mina Alibeigi, Christos Dimitrakakis
description: Abstract . In stochastic games with incomplete information, the uncertainty is evoked by the lack of knowledge about a player’s own and the other players’ types, i.e. the utility function and the policy space, and also the inherent stochasticity of different players’ interactions.

title: Daniel Green and Yiwen Huang
description: Abstract A Flat Space Analogue for the Quantum Origin of Structure Department of Physics,University of California at San Diego, La Jolla, CA 92093, USA Abstract The analytic structure of non-Gaussian correlators in inflationary cosmologies has recently been proposed as a test of the quantum origin of structure in the universe.

title: Scalar-mediated dark matter model at colliders and gravitational wave detectors – A White paper for Snowmass 2021
creator: Jia Liu, Xiao-Ping Wang, Ke-Pan Xie
description: Abstract The weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) have been the most popular particle dark matter (DM) candidate for the last several decades, and it is well known that WIMP can be probed via the direct, indirect and collider experiments. However, the direct and indirect signals are highly suppressed in some scalar-mediated DM models, e.g.

title: Consonant-Vowel Transition Models Based on Deep Learning for Objective Evaluation of Articulation
creator: Vikram C. Mathad, Julie M. Liss, Kathy Chapman, Nancy Scherer, Visar Berisha
description: Abstract Spectro-temporal dynamics of consonant-vowel (CV) transition regions are considered to provide robust cues related to articulation. In this work, we propose an objective measure of precise articulation, dubbed the objective articulation measure (OAM), by analyzing the CV transitions segmented around vowel onsets.

title: Singular symplectic spaces and holomorphic membranes Thanks: Research is supported in part by the SNSF-grants 200400, 204125 and CNPq-grant PQ 315747. The paper was written during the research visit of the second-named author to the Euler International Mathematical Institute in St. Petersburg, parti
creator: Sergey Galkin and Grigory Mikhalkin
description: Abstract . We set up a topological framework for degenerations of symplectic manifolds into singular spaces paying a special attention to the behavior of Lagrangian manifolds and their (holomorphic) membranes. We show that degenerations into singular toric varieties provide a source of exotic Lagrangian tori. 1.

title: Time evolution of superoscillations for the Schrödinger equation on ℝ ∖ { 0 } \mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}
creator: Peter Schlosser
description: Abstract . In the context of quantum mechanics superoscillations, or the more general supershifts, appear as initial conditions of the time dependent Schrödinger equation. Already in [ 5 ] a unified approach was developed, which yields time persistence of the supershift property under certain holomorphicity and growth assumptions on the corresponding Green’s function.

title: CCR and CAR algebras are connected via a path of Cuntz-Toeplitz algebras
creator: Alexey Kuzmin
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexey Kuzmin. For q ∈ ℝ q\in\mathbb{R} , | q | < 1 |q|<1 we consider the universal enveloping C ∗ C^{*} -algebra of a ∗ * -algebra of q q -canonical commutation relations ( q q -CCR), which is generated by a 1 , … , a n a_{1},\ldots,a_{n} subject to the relations a i ∗ ​ a j = δ i ​ j ​ 1 + q ​ a j ​ a i ∗ . a_{i}^{*}a_{j}=\delta_{ij}1+qa_{j}a_{i}^{*}.

title: Sampling Complexity of Path Integral Methods for Trajectory Optimization
creator: Hyung-Jin Yoon, Chuyuan Tao, Hunmin Kim, Naira Hovakimyan, Petros Voulgaris
description: Abstract The use of random sampling in decision-making and control has become popular with the ease of access to graphic processing units that can generate and calculate multiple random trajectories for real-time robotic applications. In contrast to sequential optimization, the sampling-based method can take advantage of parallel computing to maintain constant control loop frequencies.

title: Magneto-Seebeck effect in bismuth
creator: Felix Spathelf, Benoît Fauqué, Kamran Behnia
description: Abstract Thermoelectricity was discovered almost two centuries ago in bismuth. The large and negative Seebeck coefficient of this semimetal remains almost flat between 300 K and 100 K. This striking feature can be understood by considering the ratio of electron and hole mobilities and the evolution of their equal densities with temperature.

title: Wire metamaterial filled metallic resonators Preprint: APS/123-QED
creator: Rustam Balafendiev, Constantin Simovski, Alexander J. Millar, Pavel Belov
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rustam Balafendiev, Constantin Simovski, Alexander J. Millar, Pavel Belov. In this work we study electromagnetic properties of a resonator recently suggested for the search of axions — a hypothetical candidate to explain dark matter. A wire medium loaded resonator (called a plasma haloscope when used to search for dark matter) consists of a box filled with a dense array of parallel wires electrically connected to top and bottom walls.

title: The Role of Disk Winds in the Evolution and Dispersal of Protoplanetary Disks
creator: Ilaria Pascucci, Sylvie Cabrit, Suzan Edwards, Uma Gorti, Oliver Gressel, Takeru Suzuki
description: Abstract The assembly and architecture of planetary systems strongly depend on the physical processes governing the evolution and dispersal of protoplanetary disks. Since Protostars and Planets VI, new observations and theoretical insights favor disk winds as being one of those key processes.

title: The Origin and Evolution of Multiple Star Systems
creator: Stella S. R. Offner 1, Maxwell Moe 2, Kaitlin M. Kratter 2, Sarah I. Sadavoy 3, Eric L. N. Jensen 4, John J. Tobin 5
description: Abstract Observational advances over the last decade have enabled high-resolution, interferometric studies of forming multiple systems, statistical surveys of multiplicity in star-forming regions, and new insights into disk evolution and planetary architectures in these systems. In this review, we compile the results of observational and theoretical studies of stellar multiplicity.

title: I Know Therefore I Score: Label-Free Crafting of Scoring Functions using Constraints Based on Domain Expertise
creator: Ragja Palakkadavath Sarath Sivaprasad Shirish Karande Niranjan Pedanekar
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ragja Palakkadavath Sarath Sivaprasad Shirish Karande Niranjan Pedanekar. Several real-life applications require crafting concise, quantitative scoring functions (also called rating systems) from measured observations. For example, an effectiveness score needs to be created for advertising campaigns using a number of engagement metrics. Experts often need to create such scoring functions in the absence of labelled data, where the scores need to reflect business insights and rules as understood by the domain experts.

title: Snowmass2021 Theory Frontier: Theory Meets the Lab
creator: Rouven Essig, Yonatan Kahn, Simon Knapen, Andreas Ringwald, and Natalia Toro
description: Abstract We review how theorists have been instrumental in launching and developing new experiments in the last decade, and comment on the challenges and opportunities for this program to continue to thrive going forward. This whitepaper is a solicited contribution to the Snowmass2021 Theory Frontier.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Guided Graph Neural Networks for Brain Network Analysis Journal: Neural Networks
creator: Xusheng Zhao, Jia Wu, Hao Peng, Amin Beheshti, Jessica J.M. Monaghan, David McAlpine, Heivet Hernandez-Perez, Mark Dras, Qiong Dai, Yangyang Li, Philip S. Yu, Lifang He
description: Abstract Capturing brain networks’ structural information and hierarchical patterns is essential for understanding brain functions and disease states. Recently, the promising network representation learning capability of graph neural networks (GNNs) has prompted methods for brain network analysis to be proposed.

title: AlignTransformer: Hierarchical Alignment of Visual Regions and Disease Tags for Medical Report Generation
creator: Di You 1, Fenglin Liu 1 ⋆, Shen Ge 2, Xiaoxia Xie 3, Jing Zhang 3, Xian Wu 2
description: Abstract Recently, medical report generation, which aims to automatically generate a long and coherent descriptive paragraph of a given medical image, has received growing research interests. Different from the general image captioning tasks, medical report generation is more challenging for data-driven neural models.

title: Shorter quantum circuits via single-qubit gate approximation
creator: Vadym Kliuchnikov, Kristin Lauter, Romy Minko, Adam Paetznick, Christophe Petit
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vadym Kliuchnikov, Kristin Lauter, Romy Minko, Adam Paetznick, Christophe Petit. We give a novel procedure for approximating general single-qubit unitaries from a finite universal gate set by reducing the problem to a novel magnitude approximation problem, achieving an immediate improvement in sequence length by a factor of 7/9. Extending the work of [ Has17 , Cam17 ] , we show that taking probabilistic mixtures of channels to solve fallback [ BRS15a ] and magnitude approximation problems saves factor of two in approximation costs.

title: Architectures of Compact Multi-planet Systems: Diversity and Uniformity
creator: Lauren M. Weiss, Sarah C. Millholland, Erik A. Petigura, Fred C. Adams, Konstantin Batygin, Anthony M. Bloch, Christoph Mordasini
description: Abstract “I do not believe that even in a snowflake this ordered pattern exists at random.” – Johannes Kepler One of the most important developments in exoplanet science in the past decade is the discovery of multi-planet systems with sub-Neptune-sized planets interior to 1 AU.

title: Einstein field equation, recursion operators, Noether and master symmetries in conformable Poisson manifolds
creator: Mahouton Norbert Hounkonnou
description: Abstract Abstract: We show that a Minkowski phase space endowed with a bracket relatively to a conformable differential realizes a Poisson algebra, confering a bi-Hamiltonian structure to the resulting manifold. We infer that the related Hamiltonian vector field is an infinitesimal Noether symmetry, and compute the corresponding deformed recursion operator.

title: Quantum Dropout: On and Over the Hardness of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
creator: Zhenduo Wang(王朕铎), Pei-Lin Zheng, Biao Wu(吴飙), Yi Zhang
description: Abstract A combinatorial optimization problem becomes very difficult in situations where the energy landscape is rugged, and the global minimum locates in a narrow region of the configuration space. When using the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to tackle these harder cases, we find that difficulty mainly originates from the QAOA quantum circuit instead of the cost function.

title: Standard Model Predictions for Rare K K and B B Decays without | V c ​ b | |V_{cb}| and | V u ​ b | |V_{ub}| Uncertainties Submitted also to the DISCRETE2020-2021 Conference
creator: Andrzej J. Buras
description: Abstract The persistent tensions between inclusive and exclusive determinations of | V c ​ b | |V_{cb}| and | V u ​ b | |V_{ub}| weaken the power of theoretically clean rare K K and B B decays in the search for new physics (NP).

title: Radiation, entanglement and islands from a boundary local quench Preprint: QMUL-PH-22-10, SAGEX-22-23-E
creator: Lorenzo Bianchi 1,2, Stefano De Angelis 3, Marco Meineri 4
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Bianchi 1,2, Stefano De Angelis 3, Marco Meineri 4. We study the entanglement and the energy density of the radiation emitted after a local quench in a boundary conformal field theory. We use the operator product expansion (OPE) to predict the early- and late-time behavior of the entanglement entropy and we find, under mild assumptions, a universal form for the leading term, which we test on some treatable two-dimensional examples.

title: THE TURN-DOWN OF THE BARYONIC TULLY-FISHER RELATION AND CHANGING BARYON FRACTION AT LOW GALAXY MASSES This research made use of Astropy, a community-developed core Python package for Astronomy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013a ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013b ) , and Colossus ( Diemer 2018 )
creator: Kristen. B. W. McQuinn, Elizabeth A. K. Adams, John M. Cannon, Jackson Fuson, Evan D. Skillman, Alyson Brooks, Katherine L. Rhode, Martha P. Haynes, John L. Inoue, Joshua Marine, John. J. Salzer, Anjana K. Talluri
description: Abstract The ratio of baryonic-to-dark matter in present-day galaxies constrains galaxy formation theories and can be determined empirically via the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (BTFR), which compares a galaxy’s baryonic mass ( M b ​ a ​ r ​ y M_{bary} ) to its maximum rotation velocity ( V m ​ a ​ x V_{max} ).

title: Non-local computation of quantum circuits with small light cones
creator: Kfir Dolev, Sam Cree
description: Abstract The task of non-local quantum computation requires implementation of a unitary on n n qubits between two parties with only one round of communication, ideally with minimal pre-shared entanglement. We introduce a new protocol that makes use of the fact that port-based teleportation costs much less entanglement when done only on a small number of qubits at a time.

title: Targeted large mass ratio numerical relativity surrogate waveform model for GW190814
creator: Jooheon Yoo, Vijay Varma, Matthew Giesler, Mark A. Scheel, Carl-Johan Haster, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Lawrence E. Kidder, Michael Boyle
description: Abstract Gravitational wave observations of large mass ratio compact binary mergers like GW190814 highlight the need for reliable, high-accuracy waveform templates for such systems. We present NRHybSur2dq15 , a new surrogate model trained on hybridized numerical relativity (NR) waveforms with mass ratios q ≤ 15 q\leq 15 , and aligned spins | χ 1 ​ z | ≤ 0.

title: On the role of Lip Articulation in Visual Speech Perception
creator: Zakaria Aldeneh \sthanks Authors contributed equally., Masha Fedzechkina ∗ , Skyler Seto, Katherine Metcalf, Miguel Sarabia, Nicholas Apostoloff, Barry-John Theobald
description: Abstract Generating realistic lip motion from audio to simulate speech production is critical for driving natural character animation. Previous research has shown that traditional metrics used to optimize and assess models for generating lip motion from speech are not a good indicator of subjective opinion of animation quality.

title: A matching design for augmenting a randomized clinical trial with external control Publication type: Article Type
creator: Jianghao Li, Yu Du, Huayu Liu, Yanyao Yi*
description: Abstract The use of information from real world to assess the effectiveness of medical products is becoming increasingly popular and more acceptable by regulatory agencies. According to a strategic real-world evidence framework published by U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a hybrid randomized controlled trial that augments internal control arm with real-world data is a pragmatic approach worth more attention.

title: Explaining the hints for lepton flavour universality violation with three 𝑺 𝟐 S_{2} leptoquark generations Preprint: MPP-2022-30, PSI-PR-22-07, ZU-TH 08/22
creator: Andreas Crivellin, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​ and ​ Luc Schnell
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andreas Crivellin, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​ and ​ Luc Schnell. Leptoquarks are prime candidates for explaining the intriguing hints for lepton flavour universality violation. In particular, the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) L SU(2)_{L} doublet of scalar leptoquarks S 2 S_{2} is capable of providing an explanation for the tensions between the measurements and the Standard Model predictions in ( g − 2 ) μ (g-2)_{\mu} , b → s ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − b\to s\ell^{+}\ell^{-} and b → c

title: An Ultraluminous Supersoft Source in a Dwarf Galaxy of Abell 85: An Intermediate-Mass Black Hole Candidate Journal: ApJ
creator: Marko Mićić, Jimmy A. Irwin, Dacheng Lin
description: Abstract We study a large sample of dwarf galaxies using archival Chandra X-ray observations, with the aim of detecting accreting intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs). IMBHs are expected to inhabit dwarf galaxies and to produce specific signatures in terms of luminosity and X-ray spectra.

title: Zipper Codes Thanks: Submitted for publication on March 16, 2022; revised on June 15, 2022; accepted on July 19, 2022. A. Y. Sukmadji and F. R. Kschischang are with the Edward S. Rogers Sr. Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Toronto, Canada. U. Martínez-Peñas is with the
creator: Alvin Y. Sukmadji, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Umberto Martínez-Peñas, Member, IEEE, and
description: Abstract Zipper codes are a framework for describing spatially-coupled product-like codes. Many well-known codes, such as staircase codes and braided block codes, are subsumed into this framework. New types of codes such as tiled diagonal and delayed diagonal zipper codes are introduced along with their software simulation results.

title: Probing Factually Grounded Content Transfer with Factual Ablation
creator: Peter West Chris Quirk Michel Galley Yejin Choi
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Peter West Chris Quirk Michel Galley Yejin Choi. Despite recent success, large neural models often generate factually incorrect text. Compounding this is the lack of a standard automatic evaluation for factuality–it cannot be meaningfully improved if it cannot be measured. Grounded generation promises a path to solving both of these problems: models draw on a reliable external document ( grounding ) for factual information, simplifying the challenge of factuality.

title: EzGP: Easy-to-Interpret Gaussian Process Models for Computer Experiments with Both Quantitative and Qualitative Factors Thanks: Submitted on September 19, 2019.
creator: Qian Xiao, Abhyuday Mandal, C. Devon Lin, Xinwei Deng
description: Abstract Computer experiments with both quantitative and qualitative (QQ) inputs are commonly used in science and engineering applications. Constructing desirable emulators for such computer experiments remains a challenging problem. In this article, we propose an easy-to-interpret Gaussian process (EzGP) model for computer experiments to reflect the change of the computer model under the different level combinations of qualitative factors.

title: Fundamentals in Peaceman Model for Well-Block radius For Non-Linear Flows Near Well
creator: A. Ibraguimov 1 , E. Zakirov. 2 , I. Indrupskiy 3 , D. Anikeev 4
description: Abstract . We consider sewing machinery between finite difference and analytical solutions defined at different scale: far away and near source of the perturbation of the flow. One of the essences of the approach is that coarse problem and boundary value problem in the proxy of the source model two different flows.

title: Subreddit Links Drive Community Creation and User Engagement on Reddit
creator: Rachel Krohn, Tim Weninger
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rachel Krohn, Tim Weninger. On Reddit, individual subreddits are used to organize content and connect users. One mode of interaction is the subreddit link , which occurs when a user makes a direct reference to a subreddit in another community. Based on the ubiquity of these references, we have undertaken a study on subreddit links on Reddit, with the goal of understanding their impact on both the referenced subreddit, and on the subreddit landscape as a whole.

title: Inifinite Horizon Reach-Avoid Zero-Sum Games via Deep Reinforcement Learning
creator: Jingqi Li, Donggun Lee, Somayeh Sojoudi, Claire J. Tomlin
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the infinite-horizon reach-avoid zero-sum game problem, where the goal is to find a set in the state space, referred to as the reach-avoid set , such that the system starting at a state therein could be controlled to reach a given target set without violating constraints under the worst-case disturbance.

title: Characterizing Alternative Monetization Strategies on YouTube CCS: Human-centered computing Collaborative and social computing CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social computing
creator: Yiqing Hua, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Thomas Ristenpart, Robert West, Mor Naaman
description: Abstract . One of the key emerging roles of the YouTube platform is providing creators the ability to generate revenue from their content and interactions. Alongside tools provided directly by the platform, such as revenue-sharing from advertising, creators co-opt the platform to use a variety of off-platform monetization opportunities.

title: Orbital physics: glorious past, bright future
creator: D. I. Khomskii
description: Abstract Transition metal (TM) compounds present a very big class of materials with quite diverse properties. There are among them insulators, metals, systems with insulator–metal transitions; most magnetic systems are TM compounds; there are among them also (high- T c T_{c} ) superconductors.

title: Planar Rooted Phylogenetic Networks
creator: Vincent Moulton, Taoyang Wu
description: Abstract A rooted phylogenetic network is a directed acyclic graph with a single root, whose sinks correspond to a set of species. As such networks are useful for representing the evolution of species that have undergone reticulate evolution, there has been great interest in developing the theory behind and algorithms for constructing them.

title: Closing the Generalization Gap of Cross-silo Federated Medical Image Segmentation
creator: An Xu, Wenqi Li, Pengfei Guo, Dong Yang, Holger Roth, Ali Hatamizadeh, Can Zhao, Daguang Xu, Heng Huang, Ziyue Xu
description: Abstract Cross-silo federated learning (FL) has attracted much attention in medical imaging analysis with deep learning in recent years as it can resolve the critical issues of insufficient data, data privacy, and training efficiency. However, there can be a generalization gap between the model trained from FL and the one from centralized training.

title: A Closer Look at Knowledge Distillation with Features, Logits, and Gradients
creator: Yen-Chang Hsu, James Smith, Yilin Shen, Zsolt Kira, Hongxia Jin
description: Abstract Knowledge distillation (KD) is a substantial strategy for transferring learned knowledge from one neural network model to another. A vast number of methods have been developed for this strategy. While most method designs a more efficient way to facilitate knowledge transfer, less attention has been put on comparing the effect of knowledge sources such as features, logits, and gradients.

title: A Geometric Interpretation of Ranicki Duality
creator: Frank Connolly
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Frank Connolly. Consider a commutative ring R R and a simplicial map, X ​ ⟶ 𝜋 ​ K , X\overset{\pi}{\longrightarrow}K, of finite simplicial complexes. The simplicial cochain complex of X X with R R coefficients, Δ ∗ ​ X , \Delta^{*}X, then has the structure of an ( R , K ) (R,K) chain complex, in the sense of Ranicki [ 15 ] .

title: Stochastic and a posteriori optimization to mitigate coil manufacturing errors in stellarator design
creator: Florian Wechsung, Andrew Giuliani, Matt Landreman, Antoine Cerfon, Georg Stadler
description: Abstract It was recently shown in [Wechsung et. al., Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA, 2022] that there exist electromagnetic coils that generate magnetic fields which are excellent approximations to quasi-symmetric fields and have very good particle confinement properties. Using a Gaussian process based model for coil perturbations, we investigate the impact of manufacturing errors on the performance of these coils.

title: On the basis set selection for molecular core-level G ​ W GW calculations
creator: Daniel Mejia-Rodriguez, Alexander Kunitsa, Edoardo Aprà, Niranjan Govind
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniel Mejia-Rodriguez, Alexander Kunitsa, Edoardo Aprà, Niranjan Govind. The G ​ W GW approximation has been recently gaining popularity among the method for simulating molecular core-level X-ray photoemission spectra. Traditionally, G ​ W GW core-level binding energies have been computed using either the cc-pV n n Z or def2- n n ZVP basis set families, extrapolating the obtained results to the complete basis set limit, followed by a an element-specific relativistic correction. Despite of achieving good accuracy, these binding energies are chronically underestimated.

title: Privacy-Preserving Reinforcement Learning Beyond Expectation
creator: Arezoo Rajabi, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Abdullah Al Maruf, Radha Poovendran
description: Abstract Cyber and cyber-physical systems equipped with machine learning algorithms such as autonomous cars share environments with humans. In such a setting, it is important to align system (or agent) behaviors with the preferences of one or more human users. We consider the case when an agent has to learn behaviors in an unknown environment.

title: On the Hilbert-Samuel Coefficients of Frobenius Powers of an ideal Thanks: The second author is supported by Fulbright-Nehru Postdoctoral Research Fellowship. Thanks: Key words and phrases : Hilbert-Samuel coefficients, Hilbert-Kunz function, Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity, Frobenius power, face ring of
creator: Arindam Banerjee, Kriti Goel, J. K. Verma
description: Abstract . We provide suitable conditions under which the asymptotic limit of the Hilbert-Samuel coefficients of the Frobenius powers of an 𝔪 \displaystyle{\mathfrak{m}} -primary ideal exists in a Noetherian local ring ( R , 𝔪 ) \displaystyle(R,{\mathfrak{m}}) with prime characteristic p > 0 . \displaystyle p>0.

title: Quantifying Disorder One Atom at a Time Using an Interpretable Graph Neural Network Paradigm
creator: James Chapman, Tim Hsu, Xiao Chen, Tae Wook Heo, Brandon C. Wood
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by James Chapman, Tim Hsu, Xiao Chen, Tae Wook Heo, Brandon C. Wood. Quantifying the level of atomic disorder within materials is critical to understanding how evolving local structural environments dictate performance and durability. Here, we leverage graph neural networks to define a physically interpretable metric for local disorder. This metric encodes the diversity of the local atomic configurations as a continuous spectrum between the solid and liquid phases, quantified against a distribution of thermal perturbations.

title: Study of Electroweak Phase Transition in Exotic Higgs Decays at the CEPC
creator: Zhen Wang, Xuliang Zhu, Elham E Khoda, Shih-Chieh Hsu, Nikolaos Konstantinidis, Ke Li, Shu Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Yanda Wu, Yuwen E. Zhang
description: Abstract A strong first-order electroweak phase transition (EWPT) can be induced by light new physics weakly coupled to the Higgs. This study focuses on a scenario in which the first-order EWPT is driven by a light scalar s s with a mass between 15-60 GeV.

title: Measuring UID Smuggling in the Wild Conference: ; conference TBD; date TBD Internet Measurement Conference (IMC ’22), October 25–27, 2022, Nice, France
creator: Audrey Randall, Peter Snyder, Alisha Ukani, Alex Snoeren, Geoffrey M. Voelker, Stefan Savage, Aaron Schulman
description: Abstract . This work presents a systematic study of UID smuggling, an emerging tracking technique that is designed to evade browsers’ privacy protections. Browsers are increasingly attempting to prevent cross-site tracking by partitioning the storage where trackers store user identifiers (UIDs). UID smuggling allows trackers to synchronize UIDs across sites by inserting UIDs into users’ navigation requests.

title: Analysis and Adaptation of YOLOv4 for Object Detection in Aerial Images
creator: Aryaman Singh Samyal, Akshatha K R, Soham Hans, Karunakar A K, Satish Shenoy B
description: Abstract The recent and rapid growth in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) deployment for various computer vision tasks has paved the path for numerous opportunities to make them more effective and valuable. Object detection in aerial images is challenging due to variations in appearance, pose, and scale.

title: A Mass Formula For Artin–Schreier Curves Over Finite Fields
creator: Anne M. Ho, Rachel Pries
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Anne M. Ho, Rachel Pries. We study a mass formula for Artin–Schreier curves of genus g g defined over a finite field k k of characteristic p p . For an odd prime p p and for small g g , we determine the number of k k -isomorphism classes of Artin–Schreier curves of genus g g , weighted by the order of the centralizer of the Artin–Schreier involution in the automorphism group.

title: Clustering in laboratory and numerical turbulent swirling flows
creator: Sofía Angriman 1,2, Amélie Ferran 3,4, Florencia Zapata 1,2, Pablo J. Cobelli 1,2, Martin Obligado 3, Pablo D. Mininni 1,2
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sofía Angriman 1,2, Amélie Ferran 3,4, Florencia Zapata 1,2, Pablo J. Cobelli 1,2, Martin Obligado 3, Pablo D. Mininni 1,2. We study the three-dimensional clustering of velocity stagnation points, of nulls of the vorticity and of the Lagrangian acceleration, and of inertial particles in turbulent flows at fixed Reynolds numbers, but under different large-scale flow geometries. To this end, we combine direct numerical simulations of homogeneous and isotropic turbulence and of the Taylor-Green flow, with particle tracking velocimetry in a von Kármán experiment.

title: Inferring topological transitions in pattern-forming processes with self-supervised learning
creator: Marcin Abram, Keith Burghardt, Greg Ver Steeg, Aram Galstyan, Remi Dingreville
description: Abstract The identification and classification of transitions in topological and microstructural regimes in pattern-forming processes are critical for understanding and fabricating microstructurally precise novel materials in many application domains. Unfortunately, relevant microstructure transitions may depend on process parameters in subtle and complex ways that are not captured by the classic theory of phase transition.

title: Volkit: A Performance-Portable Computer Vision Library for 3D Volumetric Data
creator: Stefan Zellmann, Giovanni Aguirre, Jürgen P. Schulze
description: Abstract We present volkit, an open source library with high performance implementations of image manipulation and computer vision algorithms that focus on 3D volumetric representations. Volkit implements a cross-platform, performance-portable API targeting both CPUs and GPUs that defers data and resource movement and hides them from the application developer using a managed API.

title: Emulating Quantum Dynamics with Neural Networks via Knowledge Distillation
creator: Yu Yao, Chao Cao, Stephan Haas, Mahak Agarwal, Divyam Khanna, Marcin Abram
description: Abstract High-fidelity quantum dynamics emulators can be used to predict the time evolution of complex physical systems. Here, we introduce an efficient training framework for constructing machine learning-based emulators. Our approach is based on the idea of knowledge distillation and uses elements of curriculum learning. It works by constructing a set of simple, but rich-in-physics training examples (a curriculum).

title: Cost Function Learning in Memorized Social Networks with Cognitive Behavioral Asymmetry
creator: Yanbing Mao, Jinning Li, Naira Hovakimyan, Tarek Abdelzaher, Christian Lebiere
description: Abstract This paper investigates the cost function learning in social information networks, wherein the human memory and cognitive bias are explicitly taken into account. We first propose a model for social information-diffusion dynamics, with a focus on systematic modeling of asymmetric cognitive bias represented by confirmation bias and novelty bias.

title: A Walking Space Robot for On-Orbit Satellite Servicing: The ReCoBot
creator: Stefan Scherzinger, Jakob Weinland, Robert Wilbrandt, Pascal Becker, Arne Roennau, Rüdiger Dillmann
description: Abstract A key factor in the economic efficiency of satellites is their availability in orbit. Replacing standardized building blocks, such as empty fuel tanks or outdated electronic modules, could greatly extend the satellites’ lifetime. This, however, requires flexible robots that can locomote on the surface of these satellites for optimal accessibility and manipulation.

title: Incentive Compatibility in Two-Stage Repeated Stochastic Games
creator: Bharadwaj Satchidanandan, Munther A. Dahleh
description: Abstract We address mechanism design for two-stage repeated stochastic games — a novel setting using which many emerging problems in next-generation electricity markets can be readily modeled. We introduce a new notion of equilibrium called Dominant Strategy Non-Bankrupting Equilibrium (DNBE) which requires players to make very little assumptions about the behavior of other players to employ their equilibrium strategy.

title: Coordinated Pose Control of Mobile Manipulation with an Unstable Bikebot Platform Thanks: This work was partially supported by the US National Science Foundation under award CNS-1932370.
creator: Feng Han, Alborz Jelvani, Jingang Yi, Tao Liu
description: Abstract Bikebot manipulation has advantages of the single-track robot mobility and manipulation dexterity. We present a coordinated pose control of mobile manipulation with the stationary bikebot. The challenges of the bikebot manipulation include the limited steering balance capability of the unstable bikebot and kinematic redundancy of the manipulator.

title: Convergence error analysis of reflected gradient Langevin dynamics for non-convex constrained optimization
creator: Kanji Sato, Akiko Takeda, Reiichiro Kawai, Taiji Suzuki
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kanji Sato, Akiko Takeda, Reiichiro Kawai, Taiji Suzuki. Gradient Langevin dynamics and a variety of its variants have attracted increasing attention owing to their convergence towards the global optimal solution, initially in the unconstrained convex framework while recently even in convex constrained non-convex problems. In the present work, we extend those frameworks to non-convex problems on a non-convex feasible region with a global optimization algorithm built upon reflected gradient Langevin dynamics and derive its convergence rates.

title: An Exploratory Study on Refactoring Documentation in Issues Handling Conference: MSR ’22: Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Mining Software Repositories; May 23–24, 2022; Pittsburgh, PA, USA MSR ’22: Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Mining Software Repositories,
creator: Eman Abdullah AlOmar, Anthony Peruma, Mohamed Wiem Mkaouer, Christian D. Newman, Ali Ouni
description: Abstract . Understanding the practice of refactoring documentation is of paramount importance in academia and industry. Issue tracking systems are used by most software projects enabling developers, quality assurance, managers, and users to submit feature requests and other tasks such as bug fixing and code review.

title: Between SC and LOGDCFL: Families of Languages Accepted by Logarithmic-Space Deterministic Auxiliary Depth- k k Storage Automata 1 1 1 This exposition corrects and expands its preliminary report, which appeared in the Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Computing and Combinatorics (CO
description: Abstract The closure of deterministic context-free languages under logarithmic-space many-one reductions ( L \mathrm{L} -m-reductions), known as LOGDCFL, has been studied in depth from an aspect of parallel computability because it is nicely situated between L \mathrm{L} and AC 1 ∩ SC 2 \mathrm{AC}^{1}\cap\mathrm{SC}^{2} .

title: No Provisioned Concurrency: Fast RDMA-codesigned Remote Fork for Serverless Computing
creator: Xingda Wei, Fangming Lu, Tianxia Wang, Jinyu Gu, Yuhan Yang, Rong Chen, Haibo Chen
description: Abstract Serverless platforms essentially face a tradeoff between container startup time and provisioned concurrency (i.e., cached instances), which is further exaggerated by the frequent need for remote container initialization. This paper presents Mitosis , an operating system primitive that provides fast remote fork, which exploits a deep codesign of the OS kernel with RDMA.

title: A Class of Two-Timescale Stochastic EM Algorithms for Nonconvex Latent Variable Models
creator: Belhal Karimi, Ping Li, WA 98004, USA
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Belhal Karimi, Ping Li, WA 98004, USA. The 1 1 1 Preliminary results appeared in Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory (ISIT), 2021. Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm is a popular choice for learning latent variable models. Variants of the EM have been initially introduced by Neal and Hinton 1998 , using incremental updates to scale to large datasets, and by Wei and Tanner 1990 ; Delyon et al.

title: Online Guaranteed Reachable Set Approximation for Systems with Changed Dynamics and Control Authority
creator: Hamza El-Kebir, Ani Pirosmanishvili, Melkior Ornik
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hamza El-Kebir, Ani Pirosmanishvili, Melkior Ornik. This work presents a method of efficiently computing inner and outer approximations of forward reachable sets for nonlinear control systems with changed dynamics and diminished control authority, given an a priori computed reachable set for the nominal system. The method functions by shrinking or inflating a precomputed reachable set based on prior knowledge of the system’s trajectory deviation growth dynamics, depending on whether an inner approximation or outer approximation is desired.

title: Explicit Quantum Circuits for Block Encodings of Certain Sparse Matrices
creator: Daan Camps, Lin Lin, Roel Van Beeumen, Chao Yang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daan Camps, Lin Lin, Roel Van Beeumen, Chao Yang. Many standard linear algebra problems can be solved on a quantum computer by using recently developed quantum linear algebra algorithms that make use of block encodings and quantum eigenvalue / singular value transformations. A block encoding embeds a properly scaled matrix of interest A A in a larger unitary transformation U U that can be decomposed into a product of simpler unitaries and implemented efficiently on a quantum computer.

title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
description: Abstract Charts are very popular for analyzing data. When exploring charts, people often ask a variety of complex reasoning questions that involve several logical and arithmetic operations. They also commonly refer to visual features of a chart in their questions.

title: Representation-Agnostic Shape Fields
creator: Xiaoyang Huang, Jiancheng Yang, Yanjun Wang, Ziyu Chen, Linguo Li, Teng Li, Bingbing Ni, Wenjun Zhang
description: Abstract 3D shape analysis has been widely explored in the era of deep learning. Numerous models have been developed for various 3D data representation formats, e.g., MeshCNN for meshes, PointNet for point clouds and VoxNet for voxels. In this study, we present Representation-Agnostic Shape Fields (RASF), a generalizable and computation-efficient shape embedding module for 3D deep learning.

title: Asymmetric Fuglede - Putnam theorem for Unbounded M M -Hyponormal operators
creator: T. PRASAD, E. SHINE LAL AND P. RAMYA
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by T. PRASAD, E. SHINE LAL AND P. RAMYA. title: Halogenation induced transition of superconductor-to-semiconductor in MXene-like MOene with direct band gap and long carrier lifetime
creator: Luo Yan, Kui xue, Jing Zhang, Ruiqi Ku, Bao-Tian Wang, Liujiang Zhou
description: Abstract Traditional MXenes with intriguing mechanical and electronic properties, together with the fertilities of elemental compositions and chemical decorations have aroused much attentions. However, the semiconducting traits with direc band gap are extremetely rare among reported MXenes. Thus, broadening the family of MXene beyond carbides and nitrides with unique behaviors is still an extraordinary and fascinating field.

title: FaiRR: Faithful and Robust Deductive Reasoning over Natural Language
creator: Soumya Sanyal, Harman Singh, Xiang Ren
description: Abstract Transformers have been shown to be able to perform deductive reasoning on a logical rulebase containing rules and statements written in natural language. Recent works show that such models can also produce the reasoning steps (i.e., the proof graph ) that emulate the model’s logical reasoning process.

title: Extremal spectral radius of nonregular graphs with prescribed maximum degree
creator: Lele Liu
description: Abstract Let G G be a graph attaining the maximum spectral radius among all connected nonregular graphs of order n n with maximum degree Δ \Delta . Let λ 1 ​ ( G ) \lambda_{1}(G) be the spectral radius of G G . A nice conjecture due to Liu, Shen and Wang [On the largest eigenvalue of non-regular graphs, J.
